I instruct the Government to allocate 1 billion tenge to support the media and non-governmental organisations to explain the main provisions of socio-economic and political development of Kazakhstan until 2020. This should be realised within the framework of a state order.

Last year, from this rostrum, I proposed that all political forces in the country establish an inter-party dialogue and unite to support the country and society in a difficult period of crisis.

My initiative was supported and 7 political parties jointly developed and signed the Memorandum on Social and Political Stability in the Economic Crisis. I express my great gratitude to them for this.

This is a significant and important development. We see that during this period political rhetoric has become more balanced and criticism has become largely constructive.

This shows that peace, tranquillity and harmony in our country, where we live and raise our children, have become a national value.

Now it is time to move from inter-party dialogue to concrete actions. Ultimately, any party or public organisation works for the interests of all Kazakhstanis. Therefore, I propose that all political parties and public associations develop a new model of interaction that will contribute to the development of the country and strengthen national unity.

In practice, this will unite all political forces to work for the good of the homeland. In this work, the Nur Otan party should play a unifying role.

It is impossible to realise the ambitious tasks set before us without a unifying national strategy.

If we are to succeed, we must be guided by four basic principles:

Our main wealth is our Motherland, independent Kazakhstan!
The state and each of its citizens must not take steps that may adversely affect the stability of society and the well-being of the country.
Economic growth is a national endeavour that concerns each and every one of us. It is the key to solving society's social problems and our common success.
Integration with the regional and global market is the most important condition for development.


Dear Kazakhstanis!
It is impossible to fulfil the ambitious tasks of the future without a unifying national strategy.
If we are to succeed, each of us must proceed from the following principles:
The first is our Motherland, Independent Kazakhstan - first and foremost!
The second is that the state and every citizen refuses to take any steps, both inside and outside the country, that could have a negative impact on stability in society and on the well-being of Kazakhstanis.
Third,  economic recovery is everyone's business. This is the key to solving priority social problems, to the well-being of the whole society and every Kazakhstani.
Fourth, integration into the regional and world market is the most important condition for development.
6. Foreign policy
Kazakhstan's foreign policy course will be based on the Foreign Policy Concept.
An active, pragmatic and balanced foreign policy will be pursued to safeguard national interests, enhance the country's international standing and strengthen national, regional and global security.
Kazakhstan intends to participate in global decision-making processes in the formation of a new architecture of international relations and the contours of the world trade and financial system.
Kazakhstan will actively contribute to to establish a strategic dialogue among all existing collective security systems.
Kazakhstan fully realises its role as a responsible participant in regional and global economic processes and has been fulfilling it impeccably throughout the years of its independence.
That is why the leaders of the world's leading countries and heads of authoritative international organisations - from economic to humanitarian - consider themselves friends of Kazakhstan.
We should be proud of that.
Kazakhstan's high international reputation has enabled our country to chair the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe.
This is a great honour for us.
It is the highest responsibility to chair the OSCE at the most difficult time in modern human history
The OSCE, with its unique geographical composition of 56 participating States on three continents and a wealth of experience in co-operation among States, is one of the key mechanisms for international security and co-operation.
We have already outlined our vision for the OSCE Chairmanship.
So I won't go into detail.
Kazakhstan's Chairmanship of the most influential security organisation will be held under the motto: "Trust. Traditions. Transparency. Tolerance".
We will jointly look for ways to resolve many topical issues, develop joint mechanisms to prevent possible crisis situations.
We intend to broaden and strengthen the consensus field on fundamental security issues, as well as on the development of the Organisation itself.
We will do everything to ensure that the OSCE is a structure that recognises the diversity of the 21st century world.
Many OSCE member states supported Kazakhstan's plans, as well as my proposal to hold the OSCE Summit in Astana this year.
I proposed that the Summit discuss current security problems in the OSCE area of responsibility, the situation in Afghanistan and tolerance issues.
Our Chairmanship of the OSCE will aim to promote security and prosperity for the peoples of the world.
Dear Kazakhstanis!
Dear Members of Parliament!
As you can see, we are ready for a new stage in the development of our country. We have not yet solved such a complex and huge task.
We have carefully analysed and calculated all our options for the decade ahead.
The development programme until 2020 will be handed out to you and published in the press. We know practically by months what, where and how it will be done and built. And most importantly, as mentioned above, all our actions are backed by the necessary financial resources.
We know what difficulties await us. The global crisis is not over yet, but its acute phase has passed. As last year, I warn that force majeure circumstances may make some changes to our plans, but our general line will continue.
This is the essence and importance of our programme.
Everyone will have access to quality health care services.
Quality education from kindergarten to university will be available nationwide to every family.
The country will significantly improve the quality of housing and communal services.
Pensioners, the disabled and low-income families will be securely protected.
Young people, the foundation of our future, will be given new opportunities to build their future.
These are the new opportunities that lie ahead for each of you, for your family, for our country.
Having united for the sake of achieving our strategic goals defined by the Development Strategy until 2030, we are successfully fulfilling our mission - building an independent, prosperous and politically stable Kazakhstan.
We pin great hopes on the members of the Nur-Otan party, who need to mobilise the whole society, all members of the party to explain and implement the tasks of the coming decade, to actually lead this work and make it their programme. 
My dear compatriots!
Concluding my address to you, I would like to say: together we were able to make Kazakhstan prosperous and together we will be able to make it prosperous.
Dear compatriots!

People say: "In a country where there is unity, happiness lives".

We have elevated the greatness of the Kazakh state, established its solid foundation and glorified its name throughout the world.

We have made significant progress and surpassed the high points, but even greater heights lie ahead.

For a country like ours, with a small population and a developing economy, technology is vital. Only in this way will the world's major powers and neighbouring countries count with us.

The ultimate goal of this programme is to strengthen the independence of our country, create conditions for the development of the Kazakh people as a nation, and expand opportunities for their language and culture to flourish.

We can achieve this goal, which will determine the bright future of our descendants, only with high determination and with the unity of the people.

In recent days, I have been receiving thousands of letters and telegrams from all corners of Kazakhstan. Especially many letters come about our country's chairmanship of the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe and my work. To give you a better understanding of the mood of the people, let me read one of them:

"Dear Nursultan Abishevich, Today the Kazakh people have risen to the very top of Europe. This is the joy and pride of all Kazakh people. For us, living in the border zone, in the most remote corner of the country with a population of more than 85 thousand people, the issues of security and cooperation are of special importance. This is the main goal and aspiration of the people. When before has a Kazakh even looked through the doors of old Europe, let alone entered its main arena? May this high honour bring only prosperity to you, our people and our country.

Everything is calm here, the people live in peace, and, most importantly, the sleep of our children is not disturbed by anything. Gratitude is in our mouths, labour is in our hands, and the people's unity is growing stronger. Welfare is growing, life is moving forward day by day. Our steppes are filled with crops, our pastures with cattle, and our homes with happy families. May Allah help you in all your endeavours!

Sovet Orazaev, an honourable citizen of Raiymbek district.

Such thousands of letters coming from the south and north, west and east of our country testify to the breadth of soul of our people, their tolerance, education, deep understanding of the events taking place in the world, internal and external situation.

It is with this level of consciousness, knowledge and perseverance that we must implement this programme. It is not only the task of the President, the Parliament or the Government.

We all want to see our future bright. Then let us start this work with redoubled vigour.

Dear compatriots, I wish everyone success in this great endeavour, which will increase the glory and prosperity of our united country!

Thank you.

Title: Address of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan, Nursultan Nazarbayev, to the People of Kazakhstan
Full Text:
Through crisis to renewal and development 

Dear compatriots!
Today, the whole world is going through the difficulties of the economic crisis.
You see and know for yourself that the storm of global crisis is beginning to shake even the most powerful nations.
And we were not spared.
We have already overcome crises of various levels more than once. If we look back over the annals of our independence, it becomes obvious that building a new state on the ruins of the destroyed Soviet empire was not an easy task for us. Restoring the economy, bringing it to a new level of development - it was akin to creating something great on nothing.
But we, as a people, have met these challenges.
At the end of the last century, our independence was again put to the test during the East Asian crisis.
Thanks to timely correct decisions and effective actions, we came out of the crisis without serious losses even then.
In this way, during difficult years and challenging times, we gained experience, became stronger and tougher.
We were defining new directions for the country's development and moving forward rapidly.
Similarly, the current world crisis is a temporary phenomenon.
Our people have always remained patient and strengthened their unity in such times, saying: "Peace and death are as good as death". Any difficulties were overcome together.
The state is taking all necessary measures to prevent a crisis. Significant funds allocated from the National Fund have already started working for the smooth functioning of the domestic economy.
Social guarantees are fully preserved.
Which means it is obvious that we will also pass through this crisis without serious losses.
Crises come and go. But such values as the independence of the state, national interests and the future of our descendants remain eternal.
We have an important milestone ahead of us - the twentieth anniversary of Kazakhstan's independence.
From the point of view of the history of the world, twenty years may not be that long. But for us, it is a huge period, equal to a whole epoch.
After all, independence is the fulfilment of the dreams and aspirations of our ancestors, measured in centuries.
That is why every year of independence has a special meaning and exceptional importance for us.
In spite of any trials that our people have faced, we will continue our creative endeavours to strengthen our independence.
Thanks to the unity of all Kazakhstanis, we will be able to overcome any obstacles and reach new heights.
Be assured of this, dear compatriots!
Dear Kazakhstanis!
Dear compatriots!
For almost two decades, day in and day out, we have been creating a new country with you.
A country open and prosperous.
A country where the well-being of Kazakhstanis is improving year after year.
A country that is politically stable and has provided security for its citizens.
A country that will never be a source of external threat to anyone.
The development strategy of Kazakhstan, which was adopted for decades ahead, the experience of its implementation in the real successes of the country gave us confidence in our own strength, we were convinced of the correctness of the path we have chosen.
That is why we have developed and consistently implemented a comprehensive system of anti-crisis measures since the beginning of the crisis in the global financial markets more than two years ago.
We closely monitor the internal and external environment and take decisive action without delay. That is why the global food crisis has not become a national disaster for us.
But today, the economic crisis, which has already hit the entire global economy, continues to test our mettle.
The crisis came to us from outside. Its origins are not within the country, but are hidden in the imbalances of the world economy.
The crisis could not have been avoided and everything could not have been foreseen.
The world's leading economies have already spent more than $10 trillion to overcome it, i.e. almost 15 per cent of the world's GDP. But the situation is still not changing for the better.
The crisis has successively drawn the Americas, Europe and Asia into its orbit.
To all appearances, it will be protracted. As analysts say, the world economy has not yet reached the bottom in its decline.
I outlined my view on the processes taking place in the world in my article "Keys to the crisis". There may be different attitudes to it, but we, Kazakhstanis, have included our thought in the general search for a way out of this crisis. The crisis is not simple, the options for getting out of it should be quite different.
I am convinced that after this global crisis, the world financial system will change, and perhaps the political governance of nations. Many will come to the necessity of "manual management" of the economy, and regulation will become the most important thing to get out of this crisis.
Therefore, a deep and radical approach will help the global community find ways that will keep us safe in the next zigzags of the global market economy.
Therefore, the radical measures I have proposed will be discussed in the global community.
My proposal is a contribution to finding solutions to global problems.
But today the reality is that the contraction of business activity in the world has led to a decrease in demand for oil and metals. These are the mainstay of Kazakhstan's exports.
Over the year, the price of oil has fallen almost fourfold, and the price of metals has fallen almost twofold.
Our main trading partners and closest neighbours - Russia and Ukraine - devalued their national currencies by 40-45 per cent. And we had to devalue the tenge in the interests of our commodity producers. Otherwise, Kazakhstani products would have lost their competitiveness. We would have continued to burn the country's gold and foreign exchange reserves.
Dear Kazakhstanis!
Unfortunately, the succession of difficult trials and the power of the crisis pressure are not abating. And you should know that.
But we must be sure that we are not just prepared for these challenges.
We will cope with them and come out of this crisis an even stronger and more prosperous nation.
We will maintain our position in the global community.
By establishing the National Fund, we have pursued a targeted savings policy.
You remember well how many copies were broken - whether we should create this fund or distribute it to everyone a little bit at a time. What would we do now, when budget revenues have dropped by 20 per cent, with the payment of pensions and salaries?
When we created this fund in good times, we did the right thing. This is what States that think about their future should do.
In doing so, we have provided a safety margin for our economy against the possibility of such shocks.
To create a resilient and flexible economy, we have consistently undertaken difficult structural reforms, built up export potential and kick-started diversification.
That is why today we have a solid backlog and are able to pursue a well-thought-out and effective anti-crisis policy.
Most States responded to the global crisis by adopting economic stimulus packages.
Kazakhstan was one of the first countries in the world to react quickly to the growing turbulence of the world economy and to start implementing proactive measures.
In order to maintain the stability of the financial system, we provided banks with additional liquidity. This was done to ensure economic activity of small and medium-sized businesses and large enterprises.
The amount of guaranteed compensation for individual deposits was increased from 700 thousand to 5 million tenge. The government helped to reduce the banking sector's risks related to external borrowing and equity capital adequacy.
A total of 545 billion tenge was allocated to support housing construction and solve the problems of shareholders.
To preserve business activity in the country, we provided unprecedented financial support to small and medium-sized businesses in the amount of 275 billion tenge. The work on decisive reduction of administrative barriers continued.
A new Tax Code was enacted, which significantly reduced the rates on major taxes.
Compared to last year, corporate   income tax has already been reduced by a third this year to 20 per cent and will be 15 per cent in 2011. The VAT rate has been reduced to 12 per cent. A flat rate of 11 per cent has been introduced instead of a regressive social tax rate. Tax preferences are provided for enterprises making investments.
All this has become one of the most important incentives for the development of the non-resource sector of the economy, small and medium-sized enterprises.
The law on public procurement gives an advantage to domestic producers, which is also aimed at supporting small and medium-sized businesses.
280 billion tenge was allocated for the development of the agro-industrial complex and 120 billion tenge for the implementation of infrastructure projects.
In general, more than 2 trillion 700 billion tenge was additionally directed to the country's economy for anti-crisis purposes.
This, you will agree, is a powerful incentive to overcome the consequences of the global crisis.
We act decisively and quickly because we know when and what to do to reduce the force of the impact of the global crisis on our economy and society.
This was facilitated by the joint operational work of the Government and the Parliament of the country.
And I want you, my dear compatriots, to understand that we all together must resist the onslaught of this period.
The Government is obliged to guarantee that all state obligations to increase social payments and wages to public sector employees will be preserved in full.
As planned, public sector salaries and scholarships will be increased by 25 per cent in 2010 and by another 30 per cent in 2011.
Average pensions will be increased by 25 per cent in 2010 and by 30 per cent in 2011.
At the same time, by 2011 the amount of basic pension payments will increase to 50 per cent of the subsistence minimum.
As you know, the state supported students who were left without money to pay for their studies. In total, the state provides 11 thousand grants and 40 thousand loans for students.

Dear Kazakhstanis!
We are facing great challenges in overcoming the consequences of the crisis and preparing for subsequent economic growth.

All we have done so far is to address the current problems caused by today's crisis.
I propose not to stop, to go further and implement a new plan for further modernisation of the economy and implementation of an employment strategy to ensure the post-crisis development of the country.
In the most difficult years, we started to build and created a new capital of the country - Astana - when no one believed that we would be able to realise it. We have done it, the whole world sees it. Let us follow this good experience.
Yes, new funds are needed. To this end, I believe it is correct to allocate revenues from the commodities sector, which have traditionally been credited to the National Fund, in 2009-2010 to implement the new plan. In total, this will amount to about 600 billion tenge in addition to the already approved transfers from the National Fund.
This is a temporary but necessary measure. At the same time, we are maintaining the amount of the country's gross reserves that we have at the moment. That is 47 billion American dollars. This gives us confidence in our stability in case this crisis continues.
Another source of funds is strict savings on all budget expenditure items and strict financial discipline. With this in mind, I instruct the Government to optimise the expenditure of the republican budget and to monitor the use of budget funds on a weekly basis. This appeal is also addressed to our deputies.
The wastefulness that has already become habitual during the period of rapid growth should be replaced by reasonable consumption and economy.Let's face it, in these years, when we have money, there are more requests, the staff has been blown up and the number of business trips and various large-scale cultural days has increased. Everyone will have to think about it.
Violators of financial discipline must be severely punished in accordance with the laws of crisis times. All non-priority expenditures - administrative, investment and other - should be reduced to zero. This applies to local budgets as well.
The freed up funds will give us the opportunity, first of all, to implement the employment strategy for Kazakhstanis. It will not only help us cope with crisis shocks, but will also ensure effective economic development in the post-crisis period. It should give new opportunities to every Kazakhstani family.
The sufficiency of jobs should be the main indicator by which the ability of the members of the Government and each Akim to ensure the sustainability of the development of Kazakhstan's economy will be determined.
Every akim, every minister should know how many jobs have been cut in a week and how many we are opening on the ground. This is the basis for sustainable development.
To ensure regional employment and retraining, I instruct the Government to allocate at least 140 billion tenge.
Resources should also be allocated from local budgets to co-finance the employment strategy.
We will create new jobs for those who lose their jobs. We can provide jobs for at least 350,000 people in Kazakhstan, not counting the current public works.
We have opportunities for the development of the labour market, we do not need to invent them. This is what we are allocating the additional funds for.
Firstly, it is the reconstruction and modernisation of utility networks. These are water supply, heat supply, energy and sewerage facilities and networks.
I instruct the Government together with akims to determine the necessary costs for these purposes, to ensure not only the financing of the work, but also the strictest control over the use of every tenge allocated from the budget.
This is invisible work, we have to do it anyway. It is the basis for future development. It is an opportunity to create a huge number of new jobs in cities and locally. We will raise the purchasing power of our population. If we work cleverly, the people who are released should be retrained in new specialities.
The housing and utilities sector should have been cleaned up a long time ago. Let's do it now.
Secondly, it is the construction, reconstruction and repair of local motorways, as well as the renovation of social infrastructure, primarily schools and hospitals.
This is the task of SPKs, which are obliged to ensure maximum employment of the population. The financial side of the issue is up to the Government and akims.
We must agree now and tell the population straightforwardly: we will complete the schools and hospitals whose construction has begun. We will postpone new ones, as the situation is like this, but we will use the funds to renovate existing schools, hospitals and medical centres. Again, we will create jobs.
Also, the main motorways and railways, the construction of which we had planned, will have to be "slowed down". But the money will be used for tidying up the roads around regional centres, cities and inter-district roads. In this way, we will tighten up our rear.
Thirdly, objects of local importance in each particular locality. This may be landscaping and gardening, repair of roads, clubs or other objects at the discretion of local authorities. Targeted transfers should be allocated for these purposes.
District maslikhats, as local self-government bodies, should be allocated funds. Let them decide where to allocate these funds to solve local problems and employment issues.
I place personal responsibility for the effectiveness of this work in general on akims.
In order to implement all the above projects, we must maximise the potential of local producers. If the necessary production facilities do not exist today, they must be created, and this opens up new opportunities for business.
We are on the eve of the 20th anniversary of our independence. All over Kazakhstan, work should be deployed on how we will meet this date. These are unforgettable years for our generation, for our people. There has never been anything like this in the history of the Kazakh nation and the whole of Kazakhstan.

Therefore, we need to start this work now. I think we should give small funds, probably 50-100 million tenge, to each aul akim, so that under the control of district maslikhats they would solve current problems for the population, which is suffering some kind of disaster, issue microcredits.
In this way, we are not only solving employment issues, but also creating incentives for the emergence of new industries in our country.
Fourthly, it is the expansion of social workplaces and the organisation of youth internships.
The current Employment Act allows us to use budget funds for these purposes. In 2008, more than 13 thousand people realised their opportunities under these programmes.
Our challenge today is to expand the scope of existing programmes.
I instruct you to allocate an additional 8.6 billion tenge for these purposes. Then we will provide jobs for about 96,000 people.
At the same time, we should increase the maximum period of unemployment benefit payment from the State Social Insurance Fund from 4 to 6 months.
Our employment strategy in the context of the global crisis is aimed at full-scale retraining and retraining of personnel.
I instruct the Government together with akims to organise retraining of specialists on the basis of existing educational institutions.
Our population needs to learn, in the world people learn all their lives. In this case, there is an opportunity and necessity to retrain and get another profession that is in demand today.
We are now obliging all large construction companies to allocate funds to train people for other professions. This should be the case everywhere. If the Government and Akims organise the work normally, people will sit at desks and learn new professions.
Systemic work on retraining and retraining of personnel should pursue the following objectives.
Anyone who wants to work in a new profession should have the opportunity to learn.
Ensuring the future needs of the economy with labour resources, primarily in agriculture.
Phased replacement of foreign workers with domestic staff. We are going to cut them by half and replace them with our own.

Moreover, despite the global crisis and the difficulties of the period we are going through, we cannot afford to focus only on solving them. Our future depends on further modernisation of the economy and development of basic infrastructure.

We will continue to finance and implement existing promising investment projects.
First of all, it is the modernisation of oil refineries.
We have three oil refineries and we are still buying oils and are not provided with aviation paraffin. We need to address this now.
We must gradually fully meet our domestic demand for these petroleum products.
We will continue the construction of the petrochemical complex in Atyrau. We will finish construction of the Moynak HPP this year and continue work on the expansion and reconstruction of Ekibastuz GRES-1. Instead of eight, four units are working there. This is ready-made, low-cost electricity. We will continue work at Ekibastuz GRES-2 on the construction of the third power unit, and this year we will start construction of the Balkhash thermal power station.
Our plans include construction of the Beineu-Bozoy-Akbulak gas trunkline and reconstruction of the Western Europe-Western China road transit corridor. This year we are starting preparatory work. 5 thousand people will work there, and in 2010-2012 - up to 50 thousand people.
It will be an artery that will make Kazakhstan a transit corridor from Europe to Asia.
We started to organise production of electric locomotives, passenger and freight wagons, road bitumen, chemical industry.
I would like to make a special mention of the agro-industrial complex, thanks to the development of which we are simultaneously solving two of the most important tasks for the country - ensuring food security and diversifying exports.
Therefore, we have decided to continue   financing of investment projects to develop export-oriented industries, such as the organisation and development of dairy farms, poultry farms, feedlots, the organisation of horticultural crop production using drip irrigation, the creation of agricultural machinery assembly facilities, the development of meat processing industries, fine wool processing, and infrastructure for the export of Kazakhstani grain and its deep processing.
It is necessary to consider other significant projects for construction. This is continuation of construction of the Koksarai reservoir and other large irrigation facilities.
We had a task to introduce 60 thousand hectares of irrigated land in the Kyzylkum massif. Now it is necessary to start working on those sites where there are feasibility studies and access roads. Processing of agricultural products is the most important sector. Today we import 80% of canned fruit and vegetable products, half of meat products, 53% of milk powder. If we do all this, people from the city should go to work in the rural industry.
We estimate that export specialisation will create more than 500,000 new jobs in the long term and generate around 8 per cent additional GDP growth over the next five years.
Thus, following our strategic choice, we consistently continue to work in those sectors of the economy where we can be really competitive and occupy our niches in foreign markets.

* * *

The current difficulties are not the first challenge that has befallen us.
We overcame the deepest crisis of the transition period in the early 1990s.
Back then, the economy was collapsing at 60 per cent and inflation was running at thousands of per cent a year.
We overcame the second world crisis caused by the Asian financial markets in the late 1990s. The price of oil fell to $9 per barrel at that time. We could not pay pensions and salaries. We overcame these difficulties.
Time will pass, and we will be talking about overcoming the current crisis.
We have in our hands all possibilities to come out of the current situation with objective losses, but prepared for new growth.
Crises will recur and our goal is to learn how to manage them. So far, we have succeeded in doing so.
Today we are forced to regroup our forces and resources, and we are doing so under the influence of external circumstances. But this does not mean that we have changed our course. This course is defined by the country's Development Strategy until 2030. Life makes adjustments. But I emphasise that it is the same.
The prosperity, security and improved well-being of all Kazakhstanis remain the most important triple challenge for our State.
We have an anti-crisis plan, allocated sufficient funds from state reserves. The Government as a whole and the Prime Minister, heads of state bodies, akims are personally responsible for the implementation of planned measures to overcome the crisis.
Today's problems and the way we deal with them is a test for the maturity and stability of our society and state. I believe that we will pass this test. We have to enter a new stage of our development and multiply our achievements. I am confident that we will cope.
The unity of our people is necessary to achieve the set goals.
Therefore, I appeal to all Kazakhstanis to undertake the implementation of the above measures, to show diligence and assertiveness, to be thrifty, to help and take care of loved ones and those who need help.
I address the deputies of Parliament, Maslikhats and the Nur Otan party. The voters who voted for our party have placed great trust in us. And now, in a difficult period of crisis, we must justify it, to become at the head of a broad anti-crisis movement in society.
Together with the Government and local authorities, we need to solve specific problems of people, take special control over the implementation of anti-crisis measures and spending of budget funds allocated for these purposes.
I appeal to the Assembly of Peoples of Kazakhstan, to all political forces. Now, not in words, but in deeds, we are testing who really thinks about the people, and who does not.
Let us unite to overcome the worst crisis in the history of the planet!
Let us not embitter people, let us help them in word and deed. This is what the State is doing now. An important task remains the preservation of peace and harmony in the country.
It is because we have become an equal, independent and strong nation that we have achieved all these achievements. Our descendants should never forget that such bright days came to us solely because of independence. We must approach this special milestone in the annals of the country with full readiness. Already now we should tidy up every village, improve and green them, repair roads, decorate our houses and yards. Then the mood of the people will be lifted and the whole country will become even more beautiful!
I appeal to all civil servants. Now the responsibility of every manager to the people we all serve is increasing manifold. It is necessary to make more frequent field visits, to meet with labour collectives and the population. It is necessary to explain the measures taken by the state, to unite people, to raise them to solve problems.
I appeal to law enforcement officers. Calmness on the streets of our towns and villages depends on you. It is necessary to fight crime, corruption, fraud and violations of the law with determination and rigour. In these difficult times, we must do everything to ensure the safety of our citizens and the entire society.
I appeal to the media to show active citizenship! It is not by chance that you are called "the fourth estate"!
Now the media should act as a "counsellor" for people on how best to overcome difficulties, how to survive, how to stand up in these difficult times. We need to teach citizens on the positive experience of other people. The same role is assigned to our scientific and creative intelligentsia.
We should more often give materials that affirm such sentiments as confidence, personal activity, patience, patriotism, love for the Motherland.
Members of the Nur Otan party need to visit families more, explain what specialities can be retrained for, how to get loans and microcredits, what to do in difficult years. It is important to go round every house, every family, to become assistants and counsellors of ordinary people. Explain that there is nothing to worry about, the country is big and there is a lot of work.
So wherever we are, we must help each other, and those in the know must pass on their knowledge to those who need it.

It is this kind of mutual support that will unite our people even more!
Dear Kazakhstanis!
The success of the new stage of the country's development will largely depend on our actions and decisions.
We have the necessary resources and experience to withstand the onslaught of the global crisis. We have a clear anti-crisis programme. All the set goals are achievable!
I am confident that we will overcome all difficulties and make our Kazakhstan a strong, prosperous and respected state in the world!
Dear compatriots!
There is only one force that can defeat any difficulty - that is unity.
Just as unity is essential for the defence of one's land and homeland, it is also essential for preserving the fruits of independence and all the successes achieved.
Was it not the cohesion and unity of our people that helped us to withstand in the most difficult times, when the Kazakhs faced severe trials?
The Kazakh people, "dying a thousand times and reborn a thousand times", even during the darkest years of Soviet repression, managed to preserve their national identity thanks to unity.
When bloody conflicts broke out in other republics in the first years of independence, we were able to create and strengthen our young state, passing through the transition period without shocks, precisely thanks to consent and cohesion.
In this difficult period, I believe that my people will show unity and mutual understanding.
Be an example for others, be a support and encouragement for your compatriots. Show wisdom, patience and diligence.
We all know the folk wisdom: "As long as there is no agreement between fingers, not even a thread can be threaded through the eye of a needle".
So it's time to put aside all differences and petty strife.
It is time to unite for the sake of the country and future generations.
I wish everyone success!

Title: Address of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan Nursultan Nazarbayev to the People of Kazakhstan
Full Text:
Address of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan

H.E. Mr. Nursultan Nazarbayev

to the people of Kazakhstan

Growth of Welfare of Kazakhstan’s Citizens is

the Primary Goal of State Policy

Dear people of Kazakhstan!

My annual addresses to the people of Kazakhstan are always aimed at an analysis of our past accomplishments and future challenges, and, most importantly, at our joint search for the best way to achieve our great common goal.

In my 2006 and 2007 addresses to the nation I not only addressed today’s challenges, but also spoke about the future of our development. We should continue our strategic focus on Kazakhstan’s industrialization, on our joining the community of the world’s 50 most competitive nations and on forming a select group of 30 corporate leaders to advise on these goals.

This year I ask that the Government present a detailed report on the implementation of these initiatives.

Last year we took a further step toward the comprehensive economic, social and political modernization of Kazakhstan.

Kazakhstan entered 2008 with new economic achievements and a significantly modernized political structure.

New amendments to the Constitution enhanced the role of the Parliament and political parties, the institutions of civil society. For the first time in the history of independent Kazakhstan, parliamentary elections on a proportional basis were held. Nur-Otanwon a landslide victory, which for the first time allowed the party to appoint the Government.

Administrative reforms underway for some time have been enhanced by the introduction of executive secretariats at Government Ministries. This allows us to assure the stability of the Ministries’ valuable human resources.

Last year the economy grew by 8.5 per cent. Since 2001, the economy has been growing at an average annual rate of 10 per cent, which is quite significant.

We have been able to accumulate a considerable national reserve amounting to 40 billion US dollars, including assets of the National Fund. This significant sum played a special role in maintaining the stability of the nation’s financial system.

The social climate is also stable and favorable. Since 2000, budgetary allocations for education, health care and social security have grown more than five fold. More than five million people are covered by the government’s social security programs, twice as many as five years ago.

We are continuously increasing the amount of assistance provided to our senior citizens. The total amount of pension savings is growing steadily and has exceeded 1.1 trillion tenge.

Social infrastructure is being strengthened. 76 schoolsand 23 medical facilities were built throughout the Republic in 2007 alone.

We have managed to reverse the negative demographic trends in the country.

In three years, within the framework of the state guaranteed housing program, we have constructed more than 18 million square meters of housing. This exceeds what we had planned by 2.2 million square meters.

All these dynamic social improvements are a bright illustration of the progress of our economy, the constructiveness of our social policy and the stability of our political system.

Esteemed deputies, attendees, and guests

Nowadays, given the global market slowdown, we have to engage domestic investment resources, combined with the growing role of State-owned holding companies, development institutions, and social-cum-entrepreneurial corporations.

Notwithstanding the difficulties that have emerged, the Government has acted on my instruction to take measures toward sustainable economic growth.

We must focus on addressing short-term and medium-term objectives in the following priority areas.

First – the extractive sector.

The key vector of the oil and gas industry involves bolstering the Government's position as an influential and responsible player in the international oil and energy markets.

To that end, we have been consistently enhancing government influence in strategic energy sectors. We have already increased Kazakhstan's share in developing the Kashagan and Kumkol oil fields, the Bogatyr open-cast coal mine, and others.

This is hugely important for us, if we are to access international markets for finished products with high added value.

The efforts in these sectors must continue.

Samruk Holding Company, as well as regional SECs (Social-cum-Entrepreneurial Corporations) should undertake concrete measures for efficient development and greater competitiveness of the mining and metals sector. To that end, we must sort out the situation around the State-owned share holdings in existing mining and metal companies and transition to appropriate management of such holdings, while assuming the subsoil use rights with regard to explored iron ore and non-ferrous metal deposits, including rare metals.

The issue of exploring new deposits is to be addressed jointly with the Government.

Second– proactive infrastructure support for key sectors of the economy.

The Government must act to develop the power sector and the transportation system. Today, these sectors are clearly failing to keep up with the development of Kazakhstan's economy.

Priority tasks to provide power to the economy and the population include construction of the Balkhash Thermal Power Plant, Unit 3 of the Ekibastuz Thermal Power Plant No. 2, the Moinak Hydroelectric Power Station and others.

In 2009, construction of the second power transmission line for the North Kazakhstan - South Kazakhstan project, as well as the power transmission line from North Kazakhstanto the Aktyubinsk region must be completed. That will help reduce power shortages in Southern and Western Kazakhstan.

In order to reliably provide for gas requirements of the Republic's southern regions, theBeineu-Shymkent main gas pipeline project must be examined, and its construction started.

Specific proposals should be made on the construction of a nuclear power plant in Aktau.

At the same time, the Government ought to focus on introducing power-saving and environmentally clean technologies.

Our companies and citizens are yet to adopt power saving practices on a daily basis. We must say bluntly that cheap energy is running out. If one wants to pay less, one must save. This must be on everyone's mind.

The Government must launch this effort.

We have to provide for the construction and modernization of the railway and roadway infrastructure.

As early as this year, on a concessional basis, we should complete a railway from Shar to Ust-Kamenogorsk, start construction of railways from Mangyshlak to Bautino, from Yeralievo to Kuryk, and the section from Khorgos to Zhetigen, while starting the electrification of the Makat-Kandyagash railway section.

This year, in order to reduce rolling stock shortages, we have to draft a package of measures to develop the domestic transportation engineering sector and start implementing such measures.

We must commence actual implementation of Kazakhstan's largest transportation project, the transcontinental corridor "Western Europe–Western China", which will pass through our Southern regions and will then go to Russia via Aktobe, creating jobs and reviving the regional economies.

In order to reduce fiscal expenditures, the construction and rebuilding of highways, such asAstana–Borovoye, Astana–Karaganda, Almaty–Kapshagai, Almaty–Horgos, as well as the Greater Almaty Ring Road will commence mostly on a concessionalbasis,with an eventual introduction of tolls.

To give concession-based projects a boost and make them more attractive, the Government should improve the existing legislative and regulatory framework.

Third.The program of "30 Corporate Leaders": its implementation is helping true development of the non-commodity sectors of our economy.

As of now, over 100 projects have emerged with a claim to "breakthrough" status. Projects of vast importance to the economy are underway, such as the construction of the third gas-processing plant in Zhanazhol, mining and enrichment facilities and acopper smelter in the Aktobe region, ongoing construction of an aluminum smelter, as well as achlorine and caustic facility in the Pavlodar region, establishment of asectionrollingmill and metallurgical silicon facility in the Karaganda region, and numerous other projects.

Construction of the first integrated gas chemical complex in the city of Atyrau is to commence shortly. Next year, construction of a gas-processing plant to be supplied by the Karachaganak field, as well as a new aluminum smelter in the Kostanai region will start as well.

We will continue implementing the projects that call for establishing a tire complex in Astana, developing logistics centers in Astana and Almaty, and establishing apolycrystalline silicon manufacturing facility.

I have only mentioned the largest facilities. However, over these years, many hundreds and thousands of new enterprises have sprung up in Kazakhstan. Kazakhstan had never had a facility to produce glass, a badly needed material in high demand. Neither has Kazakhstan had an aluminum plant.

Currently, five vehicle plants are in operation, including car assembly facilities. Nowadays, radio equipment and computers are assembled in Kazakhstan. The furniture sector, construction industry, and other sectors are surging ahead.

All in all, the Program "30 Corporate Leaders" is expected to take the interaction between the Government and business to a fundamentally new level.

The performance of major ministries, the Kazyna Fund and other holdings, as well as local government offices across all levels will be evaluated, first and foremost, in terms of "breakthrough" project implementation.

* * *

The contemporary development phase is putting a number of new essential tasks on the agenda of the nation's agro-industrial complex.

Over the past five years, Kazakhstan has achieved notable results in developing its agricultural sector. Gross agricultural output has almost doubled since 2002. Investment has more than tripled. This has been made possible thanks to massive government support to the agricultural sector. You are well aware of the three-year support program for rural communities, which we have now completed. It has provided a powerful impetus.

Thanks to modern technologies used in recent years, grain crop harvests have improved dramatically.

Mandatory crop insurance, introduced in 2004, has guaranteed that farmers make money even in drought years.

These measures have contributed to the near-quadrupling of combined sales in our agriculture, which have exceeded US$4 billion.

Improving the quality of life in our villages and rural communities will remain a government priority.

Given the evolving global trends and its existing potential, the agro-industrial complex should develop into a key revenue earner for our economy.

Agricultural product prices have been rising; in general, this sector is becoming highly lucrative and we should invest in it. I am sure that rural communities will respond with impressive labor and higher returns.

First. The country's food security must be assured.

To that end, it is imperative to attract greater investment in agricultural and food processing.

Kazakhstan meets its domestic demand for key staple foods and has export potential.

Close attention must be given to providing incentives for production of essential staples that do not yet meet the nation's demand. Those include, for instance, vegetable oils, fruits, sugar, and others. We are capable of addressing these problems.

Second. It is important to focus on those agricultural sectors that export their products. In particular, the channels for grain exports via Caspian and Black Sea ports, as well as exports to China must be expanded.

Third. The livestock sector likewise offers a great export potential. In a further step, our veterinary system should transition to international standards.

I am instructing the Government to take further measures for systemic support of agriculture across all levels.

Special attention must be paid to the processing of raw materials.

* * *

Macroeconomic policy priorities.

The Government, the National Bank, and the Financial Supervision Agency must establish effective mechanisms for systemic and prompt government responses to any threats of financial instability and must bolster the international markets' confidence in Kazakhstan's economy.

First. Systemic enhancements are needed in the operations of the Financial Supervision Agency.

The primary goal of the Agency, as well as the National Bank and the Ministry of Finance, should be improving the competitiveness and stability of the nation's financial system, particularly its banking sector. Vagaries of life will call for adjustments to our plans. We should be ready for that.

We must learn the lessons of the U.S. sub-prime loans crisis, which has seriously affected our banks.

The Financial Supervision Agency should monitor the situation in each bank more closely and should employ preventive and effective measures, if need be.

Government support can not be a one-way street, and the banks should assume their portion of risks. If bank shareholders are unwilling or unable to raise extra resources for the banks' development, the Government should be ready to take necessary action.

Meanwhile, the process of regulatory intervention should be extremely transparent and predictable to the entire banking sector.

We view the advent of foreign capital to the banking sector as a vote of confidence in Kazakhstan, as a source of much-needed financial support and of best international practices in the area of banking services.

Structural reforms of our financial system must continue. These involve the development of the securities market, advanced financial instruments, improved bankruptcy legislation, and a profound reform of the judiciary.

We should develop systemic risk management in private and public sectors alike.TheGovernment, the Fiscal Supervision Agency, and the National Bank ought to construct a flexible and reliable system of risk management.

Furthermore, asystem of rapid response measures is to be developed for contingencies.

The degree of confidence on the part of the general public and the business community, including foreign business, should become a key performance criterion for the nation's financial authorities.

Second. The taxation system must be aligned with the objectives of this new phase in Kazakhstan's development. The existing Tax Code has played a positive role in supporting economic growth. However, its potential has been largely exhausted by now. The Code includes in excess of 170 exemptions and preferences which continuously proliferate on an ad hoc basis.

The Government should draft a new Tax Code designed to promote modernization and diversification of the economy while bringing business in from the shadows.

The new Code should have the character of a direct action law that prevents arbitrary interpretation of its rules by tax authorities, while combining high quality tax administration with taxpayer interests.

Most importantly, though, it should provide for areduction of the total tax burden on non-commodity sectors of the economy, particularly small and medium-sized businesses. Theexpected shortfall in government revenue should be offset by greater economic returns from the extractive sector.

Third.TheAgencyfor Protection of Competition, newly established on my instructions, is to perform a special mission of ensuring our economy's efficiency and competitiveness.

The Agency's broad powers should guarantee success in fighting collusion on prices, bad faith competition, and certain market players who abuse their dominant or monopoly status, while enhancing the positions of Kazakhstani business globally.

A new competition law is needed, to provide serious impetus for the growing entrepreneurial activity in this country.

Fourth. We should redouble our anti-inflation efforts. Given rising inflation, which is exacerbated by pressures from global economic developments, the Government should take well-considered and appropriate action.

I expect that theNational Bank, too, will achieve substantial results in the fight against inflation.

The Government should proactively control the situation in the context of global economic instability. All the necessary resources are in place.

Therefore, theGovernment and the National Bank should have an operations plan of stabilization actions in case the global economy experiences the expected slowdown and the prices of certain exports weaken.

First and foremost, until the financial sector's problems are overcome, the Government should temporarily reduce government expenditure across all areas and programs other than social ones.

All of the above-mentioned plans must follow this requirement.

Anything that can wait should be suspended. This concerns all regions, too. Such austerity will be instrumental in reducing inflationary pressures while enhancing the nation's reserves in case energy and commodity prices decline.

Esteemed attendees,

We shall continue on the path of improving Kazakhstan’s political model and system of government by combining the generally accepted tenets of democratic development and our society's traditions.

First.Over the 16 years of our independence, we have implemented our own model for securing public stability and inter-ethnic accord, molding the Kazakhstani identity and shared Kazakhstani patriotism.

This is our Kazakhstani know-how, of which we are justly proud and which we must carefully guard.

Within the Constitutional Reform context, thestatus and power of Kazakhstan’s People's Assembly have increased.

As they represent the interests of all people across our multi-ethnic nation, deputies elected by the Assembly are called upon to play a special role in consolidating inter-ethnic peace and accord in Kazakhstan.

Currently, the role of this Kazakhstan’s unique institution needs strengthening through all means available. Deputies elected by the Assembly should feel this responsibility and maintain close links with the Assembly and its local organizations.

As I have always said and as I would like to reemphasize with full responsibility, Kazakhstan needs long-term stability, peace and accord for further strengthening of the nation and its security, for sustainable economic development and for a better standard of living for our citizens.

Second.The development of a modern political system should continue in Kazakhstan.

Political parties, non-governmental organizations, and other public institutions should play the lead role in such process.

The strengthening of party mechanisms will promote the establishment of modern civil society and the general public's broad involvement in social processes.

Presently, themodel based around Nur Otan as the dominant party may be viewed as the optimal form of political system for Kazakhstan.

Thanks to this model, all other political parties are able to run in elections, get elected to the Parliament, and take part in all political developments. There are no obstacles to the emergence of new parties or to expression of one's own opinion.

Third. In the context of a democratic society, the fight against crime and corruption is assuming great significance. The past years have seen substantial improvements in the ability of the nation's law-enforcement and judiciary system to combat criminal phenomena, and to protect our citizens' lives and rights.

However, their operations are not free of significant shortcomings.

These were discussed at a recent Board Meeting of the Prosecutor General's Office in the presence of all law-enforcements authorities.

The law-enforcement system and the judiciary must assure fair and effective protection of Kazakhstan citizens' rights, while protecting business from unlawful interference.

In this area, crime preemption and prevention, rather than punitive action should be a priority. Therefore, a bill "On Prevention of Offences" must be drafted and submitted to the Parliament this year.

I am instructing the Presidential Administration to ensure the implementation of all these measures, to carry out anadministrative reform of the law-enforcement authoritiesand all entities reporting to the nation's President.

Fourth. The Government must promptly implement the measures envisaged by thisadministrative reform for the development of Kazakhstan's government administration system in keeping with the principles of effectiveness, transparency, and public accountability, and with due regard for best international practices.

These new approaches should be tried and tested in 2008 within pilot government agencies such as the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Economy and Budget Planning, the Ministry of Finance, and the Governor’s office of the South Kazakhstan region.

Greater efficiency and better performance of the administrative apparatus must be theprimary goal of the administrative reform, so that officials serve the people properly.

A new nation-wide human resources policy must become a key aspect ofadministrative reform. At the current phase of development, the human factor is becoming crucial.

Modern approaches must be developed to establish aprofessional core of new-style managers within the public administration system.

The Nur Otan party should play a major role in this process. The party should take an active part in developing human resources for the public administration system, acting as a "social elevator" for deserving citizens.

An important role should be assigned to the younger generation, including the Bolashak program graduates.

Young professionals should find their place in the developments taking place in the nation, and should take a very active part in building the future. Work with the human resource pool slated for potential promotion should be raised to a new, higher level.

The Presidential Administration must lead the human resources effort.

Fifth. As of the next year, for the first time in our nation's history, the new system of government budget planning will be based on athree year budget. To that end, the Government must draft a new Budget Code this year.

We must also redouble efforts to modernize and improve the planning system, boost the effectiveness of budget expenditure, and improve the management of government assets.

Sixth. The Government must conduct a targeted audit or, if you will, anaudit with prejudice, of government funds allocated under the Government's major socio-economic programs.

The objective of this audit is to assess performance and dramatically improve the efficiency of managing and expending government funds.

Seventh. The Government should continue its consistent efforts at providing incentives for greater competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises.

Operations of micro-credit institutions should be supported, including with public funds. Such institutions aid hundreds of thousands of our citizens in establishing their own businesses. We should devise measures to make micro-credit more accessible and create new jobs for a greater number of Kazakhstanis.

A well-developed entrepreneurial sector is the basis of any economy.

In this regard, I am instructing the Government, in theadministrative reform's context, to radically reduce the administrative burden on businesses, and to furthersimplify the approval system, mostly in terms of licensing, certification, and accreditation.

Let me offer anexample. According to the latest World Bank report "Doing Business", it takes 89 days to perform all export-related procedures in Kazakhstan, whereas it only takes five days to do the same in Estonia.

Various inspections, contemplated by more than 50 laws, have turned into a true calamity for businessmen.

Certain agencies use various pretexts to "inspect" a business several times in violation of the law. This seriously distracts enterprises from their business. Furthermore, it runs counter to the policy that I have been pursuing.

The number of inspections carried out by law-enforcement authorities and other inspectors should be significantly reduced, and such inspections should be streamlined.

Dear Kazakhstanis,

Continued improvement of the social well-being of the Kazakhstanis, all elements and social groups of Kazakhstani society have been and will remain at the forefront of government policy.

Quality-of-life standards should become an effective market-based tool for human capital development and social modernization of Kazakhstan, without giving rise to free-rider attitudes.

The Government's social policy can only be effective if it seeks to create jobs and bring the able-bodied population into the national economy. We have followed this principle until now and we intend to observe it going forward.

We have every reason to further improve the living standards of disadvantaged members of the public, in keeping with the election platform of the Nur Otan party, which has a five year horizon.

The new three-year budget should provide for:

Overall rise of average pensions by the factor of 2.5 between 2007 and 2012, including a 25% rise in 2009, a 25% rise in 2010, and a 30% rise in 2011. Meanwhile, base pension benefits should reach 50% of the subsistence level by 2011;

A 9% annual average increase in government social benefits and specialized government benefits starting in 2009;

A phased increase of the monthly child care benefit once the child reaches one year of age, to exceed the 2007 benefits by an average factor of 2.5 by 2010-2011;

An increase of one-offbenefits for the birth of the 4th child and more, in excess of 4 times the 2007 amount, starting as of 2010;

Salary increases for government employees, to gradually double salaries by 2012, including a 25% increase in 2009, a 25% raise in 2010, and a 30% raise in 2011.

In 2009, the annual quota for resettlement of Oralmans to their historical homeland should be raised by 5 thousand families to 20 thousand families a year.

Work in support of social wellbeing should come hand-in-hand with a higher quality of life and a higher quality of the nation's human resources. This is the primary mission of the nation's research, education, and health sectors.

* * *

The main challenge in our education system is to expand high-quality education services through the implementation of the State Program on the Development of Education through 2010.

First, I commission the Ministry of Education and regional governors to establish within three years a viable education infrastructure to provide modern education and to increase the use of advanced technologies.

This year we will complete the construction of 88 schools for 68 thousand students, and in 2009-2010 some 102 more schools for 69 thousand pupils are to be completed.

Second, I commission the Government and national entities, in cooperation with regional governors and the governors of Almaty and Astana, to develop and implement the program on the further development of professional and technical education.

This program should provide for the attraction of foreign scientists and teachers to the areas of education most useful to the national economy.

Therefore, first and foremost, employers and their associations, in other words, businesses that are in need of such well-trained human resources should be actively involved in the process.

Third, the Government should speed up the implementation of the "Unity of three Languages" cultural project. I would like to draw your attention to the urgent need to increase the quality of Kazakh language teaching, as this language unites the entire society.

Having carefully studied relevant international experience, we should develop and introduce the most advanced programs and techniques for teaching Kazakh. It is vital to develop innovative methodological and practical manuals and audio and video materials to promote the effective learning of our national language.

There are only one or two publishing houses that constantly win bids to publish textbooks in Kazakh. Do we actually have the kind of competition that contributes to the improvement of the textbooks’ quality? The quality of textbooks in Kazakh does not meet the standard. The books do not entice people to learn Kazakh, on the contrary, they push them away from the language. Relevant government agencies should take all appropriate measures to resolve this issue.

Fourth, a breakthrough in providing our citizens with preschool facilities has not yet been achieved. The Government and governors should explore the problem in detail and find an appropriate solution.

We should pay particular attention to the preschool education system, as this is the first element of continuous education for our youngest citizens. Effective programs for the development of their creative and intellectual abilities should be introduced at this stage. We should bear in mind that it is exactly at this age that their attitude towards learning, working and understanding the outside world is being formed.

Our healthcare system today does not yet meet the requirements of Kazakh citizens. This is our main challenge in the healthcare system. We are not satisfied with the current infrastructure, quality and management of medical services.

First, the Government should re-energize its work on the refurbishment and development of healthcare facilities. This year we will build nine national level healthcare facilities and 112 local facilities.

Second, taking into account that prevention is cheaper than treatment, we should review current programs with a view to increasing the use of the most advanced techniques in early diagnostics, detection and treatment. We should analyze and estimate the real price of medical services in order to assure that sufficient financial resources are allocated for healthcare.

Third, I commission the Education and Health Ministries to launch jointly a programto improve the professional skills of medical personnel through additional training and retraining, certification and licensing.

In addition, the number of grants allocated to medical universities and the quota for medical training under the Presidential “Bolashak” scholarship should be increased.

Fourth, particular attention should be paid to providing our people with medicines. The quality of imported medicines should be thoroughly scrutinized and controlled. And we need to be more active in attracting foreign investments for the construction of national pharmaceutical factories.

Fifth, it is particularly important to develop the appropriate infrastructure for the “Healthy Nation” project. We should emphasize and provide every possible opportunity for physical and sports training for our citizens from an early age.

Governors should restore existing and build new stadiums, sports facilities and athletic fields for children and adults, thus providing opportunities for exercise for citizens of all ages to get in shape and live longer lives.

Ministries and governorates should launch extensive campaigns for a healthy lifestyle.This is an issue of national importance, and the Government should approach it on a larger scale.

A package of measures must be devised for a demographic turnaround. This should be the keynote issue for the coming session of the National Council.

The nation's health is a national goal. Thedomestic businesscommunity should actively contribute to attaining this objective.

Here, I would like to note with satisfaction that the business community has actively responded to my appeal for greater social responsibility on its part.

Last year alone, such entities as Kazakhmys Corporation, the Eurasian Industrial Association, KazZink, Tengizchevroil, Agip, as well as the national companies KazMunaiGaz, Kazatomprom, and Kazakhstan Temir Joly, spent in excess of 30 billion tenge on the development of social facilities, including schools, medical and pre-school institutions, rehabilitation centers, disabled persons' rehabilitation centers, as well as culture and sports faculties.

This is avivid example of good corporate citizenship. Such practices should become common, and the media should support them.

* * *

Accessible high-quality housing for our citizens, particularly for new families, is an issue that has always been and still remains among the Government's most vital priorities.

It is high time to make the following amendments to the National Housing Program.

First. Extension of provisional housing loans at a rate not exceeding 4% per annum to government employees through a building-savings system.

Second.We should emphasize construction of rental housing, including for government employees. For the benefit of citizens wishing to build their own homes, the Government will set up a private homebuilding infrastructure.

SECs should get actively involved in this process under the program.

Third. We should legislate to ensure operational transparency of construction companies and greater competition in that sector. Greater protection should be provided to the rights of the individuals who make equity contributions to housing projects.

Simplified rules are needed for allocation and documentation of land plots in order to provide incentives to private home construction.

Fourth. The introduction of industrial, affordable, and environmentally clean technologies of private home construction should become a priority. The latest international experience should be used.

Fifth.Further development of Astana, which, this year, will mark ten years as the nation's capital, is a highly important task.

The construction of advanced transport and utilities infrastructure, as well as power sources for the capital city must continue. To secure a reliable power supply for the city, a power complex development program should be implemented along the lines of a public-private partnership, which would include the construction of Thermal Power Plant No. 3.

The Government must redouble its efforts at creating a food belt around Astana, in order to saturate the capital's consumer market and stabilize prices.

In 2008, the Government and the Astana Governor’s office are to complete the establishment of a health service cluster, making sure that all facilities are commissioned as scheduled by the capital city's 10th anniversary.

* * *

Improvement in the population's well-being should remain a priority for Governors at each and every level. Focused efforts are needed in the following areas.

First. Improved fiscal performance. We must cut back on all expenditures unrelated to the population's social well-being.

At the central level, work is already underway to implement result-oriented budgets. This work must also be expanded to the local level. The public should feel that regional authorities truly care about them.

New social facilities, such as medical institutions, schools, and sports facilities should become centers for providing the public with high quality, state-of-the-art and, most importantly, mass-scale services.

Second. The Governors must ensure proactive development of infrastructure, in particular, local roads.

Third. The practice whereby non-transparent arrangements are used for land allocation must be discontinued. All land must be allocated by way of public auctions. The only exception will apply to special-purpose land plots intended for SEC operations.

As seen from audits carried out by the Government, land around Astana and regional capitals have been bought in advance in the name of front companies and individuals. Nowadays, by selling those lands at market prices, certain persons, including quite a few officials, are getting rich at the Government's expense without having invested anything. They should be given the option of voluntarily returning such lands to the Government; otherwise, law-enforcement authorities should invesitgate whether such actions were lawful and whether such persons are liable.

It would be great if the Nur Otan party and its parliamentary faction undertook to monitor this issue.

In general, Nur Otanbranches and grassroots organizations, as well as local Maslihat deputies should become a serious factor for regional development and economic modernization. They must take an active part in implementing this package of measures and keep a close watch over the tasks enumerated above.

Esteemed Members of the Parliament,

Ladies and Gentlemen,

Since it gained its independence, Kazakhstan has become a full-fledged member of the international community whose initiatives have almost without exception received broad support and have been translated into reality.

Intergovernmental entities established at the initiative and with direct involvement of Kazakhstan have demonstrated that there was indeed a need for them. Such intergovernmental entities have laid down the foundation for an effective regional security system and include CICMA, the SCO and CSTO.

We must continue to strengthen our economic and political cooperation with Russia, China,and the Central Asian countries. We must create a firm foundation for stability, an open dialogue and interaction in the region.

We are also expanding our constructive interaction with the USA, EU, and NATO with a view to strengthening security in the Central Asian region.

As of now, this country has reached a qualitatively new level of international recognition as convincingly demonstarted by the decision to grant Kazakhstan the rotating chair at the Organization of Security and Cooperation in Europe in 2010.We are grateful to the members of that organization, especially to the CIS heads of state who have collectively nominated us for that position.

In this regard, it is necessary to devise a special program, “Path to Europe.” The program would be intended to promote economic cooperation, bring in technology and management experience, improve our legislation, develop our own agenda and a strategic vision for our chairmanship of the OSCE.

On the whole, our foreign policy and security priorities remain unchanged.

First.Our foreign policy is built on a quest for commonality of fundamental interests, understanding the need for compromise solutions to all, including the most difficult issues.

Second.Kazakhstan intends to continue strengthening, in every way, its position as an active member of the international coalition against international terrorism and religious extremism.

Third. We will continue the modernization and combat preparation of the Kazakh Army.

Over the past few years this nation’s Armed Forces have significantly enhanced theirmilitary and technical capabilities.

It is necessary to form a professional, military and command corps of the Armed Forces capable of confronting modern security challenges.

On the whole, this country’s Armed Forces are being tasked to continue to raise their combat readiness and competitiveness in accordance with the new Military Doctrine. The Government, the State as a whole must provide resolute support to our Armed Forces.

* * *

I would like to specifically note that over the next few years a number of major international events of global importance will be organized.

I am referring to the Third Congress of World and Traditional Religions in 2009, theConference on Confidence and Security Measures in Asia in 2010, work in the OSCE Troika starting in 2009, and chairing the OSCE in 2010.

Serious preparatory work, both organizational and substantive, must start now. This is a job both for the Foreign Ministry and the Government and for all government agencies.

Dear compatriots!

Members of Parliament and Government Ministers!

As you are well aware, the number of our goals increases from one year to the next. We all work for the sake of strengthening of our country’s independence and the nation’s prosperity and for improving the standard of living of our people. I am confident that we shall justify the people’s trust and reach the goals we have set for ourselves.

That’s all that I wanted to tell you today.

Thank you for your attention.

Title: Address of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan, Nursultan Nazarbayev, to the People of Kazakhstan
Full Text:
A new Kazakhstan in a new world

Dear deputies and members of the Government!
Ladies and gentlemen!
Since the first days of independence, you and I have made every effort to ensure that New Kazakhstan moves forward confidently. We have chosen our path of development, and today our country is increasingly asserting itself in the global community, gaining more and more international prestige.
