We have laid a solid foundation for the economy and statehood. The future of Kazakhstan has been worked out in detail from the economic, social, political and administrative points of view. We have confidently entered a new stage of development.
Today I would like to present to you my vision for the future of our country and society. I am confident that the realisation of our plans will give Kazakhstan the opportunity to make a historic leap forward.
Today we will talk about the steps that need to be taken to become one of the 50 most competitive countries in the world. We spoke about this in the previous Address.
Today, however, we will discuss concrete measures that will help us achieve this goal. What should every leader do, especially those in power?
You remember that in 1997 I proposed the Development Strategy of Kazakhstan until 2030. It became an important document that defined the future of our society and the great goals of our state.
At that time, we were facing huge socio-economic difficulties, we did not have sufficient experience in managing a market economy and implementing liberal reforms. And at that time, many people doubted the success of this Strategy.
However, today, ten years later, time has proven that our choice was the right one.
Thanks to him, Kazakhstan has confidently passed through the trials of a market economy and built a modern democratic state.
We have strengthened social institutions, raised living standards and achieved internal stability.
Moreover, we have become the strongest economy in the region and have taken our rightful place in the international community by making important geopolitical and peacekeeping commitments.
We have not remained among the "third echelon" countries. And this is the main result of our ten-year labour.
I am here today to set our objectives for the next 10 years.
We have completed the first decade of the 2030 Strategy. Now we must answer the question: what to do in the next decade?
Of course, within this period there will be three and five year plans to help us move towards the goal.
We promised that by 2010 we would double GDP compared to 2000. And if everything goes well, we will fulfil this task in the next few years, even two years ahead of schedule.
But our goal is not just economic growth. It is a real opportunity to improve the life of every Kazakhstani.
In recent years, we have resolved many social issues that have significantly improved the quality of people's lives.
We have increased scholarships for university and college students, provided grants and educational loans. We regularly raise the salaries of public sector workers and civil servants. We pay allowances to low-income families for children up to 18 years of age, and mothers with many children receive special state payments. We provide free medicines to children and adolescents from vulnerable categories. We increase the size of pensions every year. A differentiated approach to their calculation depending on length of service has been introduced, which has affected more than one million people. Pensions have also been increased for veterans of the security forces. All pension and social payments are made on time.
All these achievements have become possible thanks to economic growth. Today we can confidently say: a strong state is a state that uses its wealth for the benefit of the people!
Dear Kazakhstanis!
As promised, the stable development of the economy allows us to strengthen the social orientation of reforms. This is the most important outcome of our economic policy.
I am instructing the Government today to continue to work to improve the well-being of our people, building on the growth of the economy and our fiscal capacity.
Firstly, attaching exceptional importance to the social protection of motherhood and childhood, from 1 January 2008 to increase the amount of a lump-sum state benefit in connection with the birth of a child to 34740 tenge. Or twofold.
Increase monthly childcare allowances until the child reaches one year of age. They will amount to:
at the birth of the first child - almost 5,800 tenge, or an increase of 177 per cent;
at the birth of the second child - about 6,400 tenge, or an increase of 167 per cent;
at the birth of the third child - over 6900 tenge, or an increase of 159 per cent;
at birth of the fourth child and more - up to over 7,500 tenge, or an increase of 153 per cent.
The additional need for funds to support families with children will amount to 9.5 billion tenge.
The measures taken earlier have made it possible to achieve a steady increase in the population of our country. Thus, if in 2000 220 thousand children were born, in 2006 - 290 thousand. In 2005 alone, the natural growth of the population due to the birth rate totalled 121 thousand people. In general, demographic growth over the past four years has totalled more than half a million people.
I am confident that the introduction of these measures will lead to even greater positive demographic changes.
Second, introduce compulsory social insurance of pregnancy, childbirth and maternity for working women. At the same time, their pension savings should continue while they are on maternity and childcare leave for up to one year.
These benefits should be paid from the State Social Insurance Fund, formed from the redistribution of social tax.
This will require an additional 9.2 billion tenge to be allocated from the state budget.
Third, to increase the size of the basic pension and to ensure that it remains at 40 per cent of the subsistence minimum in the coming years. Thus, for the first time, we are bringing Kazakhstan's pension provision in line with international standards.
This will affect more than 1 million 675 thousand recipients of the basic pension, and its amount will increase by about one thousand tenge or more than 35 per cent in 2008. Minimum pension payments (basic plus minimum solidarity pension) will increase by about 1,500 tenge, or 15 per cent, in 2008.
Fourthly, in order to establish fairness in assigning pensions based on previous labour contribution, change the limit on income taken into account for calculating pensions provided for in the pension legislation, raising it from 15 times to 25 times the monthly calculation index.
About half a million pensioners (483,000 people) whose pensions were previously underestimated due to the legal limitation of income taken to calculate pensions will receive a significant pension increase.
The average size of the solidarity pension will exceed 13,600 (thirteen thousand six hundred) tenge, or by almost 25 per cent. The maximum size of solidarity pensions will increase in 2008 to almost 22 thousand tenge, or by 76 per cent.
Fifth, to stabilise the purchasing power of pension payments, indexation of pension payments should be maintained and carried out ahead of the projected growth of the consumer price index by two per cent.
The total requirement of funds for these activities will amount to 55.3 billion tenge.
Sixth, as you know, wages in the public sector have been raised by 30 per cent since 1 January 2007. It is necessary to continue work on further improvement of the system of labour remuneration of public sector employees.
Seventh, in order to raise their status, attract and strengthen human resources in such spheres as education, social security, health care, culture and sports, I believe it is necessary, starting from 1 January 2008, to introduce the payment of a health-improvement allowance at the time of leaving on leave in the amount of one official salary.
This will cost the budget 30.6 billion tenge in 2008 alone.
Eighth, in previous years, the issue of social security for persons who, as of 1 January 1998, had worked out their length of service in harmful and difficult working conditions was repeatedly raised.
The workers of the enterprises raised this issue with me at meetings. I know that they also put it before you, members of the Parliament. I understand them. I went through it myself. Earlier we solved the issue on List No. 1. Now we need to solve the issue of List 2. We have about 28,000 such Kazakhs. I believe that now we have the opportunity to return to solving this problem.
We can introduce special allowances for this category in the amount of eight monthly calculation indices. This will require more than three billion tenge annually. It is necessary to find these funds and from 1 January 2008 to ensure the payment of special allowances according to List No. 2.
Thus, the total need for funds to increase all the social payments I have listed in 2008 will be about 108 billion tenge.
Today, the State has an opportunity to allocate such large funds to improve the social security of Kazakhstanis. And we are realising this opportunity.
Ninth, I instruct the Government to build 100 schools and 100 hospitals within three years in those regions of the country that are in particular need of these facilities. We must make the development of social infrastructure a strategic objective.
I believe that we have come to the point where we need to form a mechanism for social and infrastructural development through public-private partnerships. We have not started this work yet. The government needs to do this.
Dear Kazakhstanis!
The consistent implementation of the Kazakhstan-2030 Strategy has provided a solid foundation for our further progress.
We have every reason to move forward even more successfully, and we will not miss our historic chance.
For this purpose, the path of accelerated comprehensive modernisation of Kazakhstan was chosen.
This is the only correct vector for our further development.
We are obliged to enter and securely establish ourselves in foreign markets in order to ensure a worthy place for Kazakhstan and Kazakhstanis in the modern world, growth of prosperity, and a significant improvement in the standard of living of the entire population of the country.
On this path we will have to, taking into account Kazakhstan and regional realities and embodying the achievements of the advanced states of the world:
First, we need to accelerate the pace of modernisation of those sectors where we have already had some success;
Secondly, to extend modernisation to all spheres of Kazakhstan's economy and social life without exception.
Therefore, as early as last year, we formulated and began work on our all-Kazakhstan project.
This is accelerated advancement into the community of fifty most competitive countries of the world and strengthening of Kazakhstan's position as its permanent member.
And the necessary condition for this is that Kazakhstan's goods and services reach a qualitative level of advanced international standards.
But this is not enough. We have to pragmatically and prudently identify and utilise our real and prospective competitive advantages at all levels of the economy - both current and potential.
Systemicism is the main formula for our accelerated advancement in the modern world in the next decade.
We have all the prerequisites for that.
We are given: a vast territory; favourable geographical and communication and transport location; availability of significant natural resources.
We have achieved: leading positions in the regional economy; constructive relations with international partners; political and socio-economic stability.
For Kazakhstan to become a truly integral and dynamic part of the world markets for goods, services, labour, capital, modern ideas and technologies, we must address ten major challenges.
The first task is not just to ensure and maintain sustainable development of the economy, but to manage its growth.
We will need to develop and implement a holistic strategy to ensure the sustainability of economic competitiveness, as well as rigorous monitoring of its implementation.
This strategy should be based on the specific competitive advantages of individual sectors and industries of our economy and take into account trends in global development and external market conditions.
We need to learn how to manage this growth, transforming it into economic development at a qualitatively new level.
We must ensure a fundamentally new approach to the industrialisation of Kazakhstan, which would meet the requirements and conditions of international markets.
We need to reduce the spheres of natural monopolies by restructuring the largest monopolists and developing competitive relations.
In the sectors of the economy where natural monopolies will remain, we will have to do serious work on tariff and technical regulation with the help of sectoral regulators.
We are obliged to reach a new level of sustainability and competitiveness of the financial system in a liberalised environment.
We need to create a stock market that works effectively.
Its development is impossible without attracting the population to actively invest their savings in securities.
The government needs to undertake a large-scale effort to adequately educate the population on the basics of investment literacy.
It would be desirable for the Government and Parliament to identify joint activities on this issue.
Accession to the WTO on terms favourable to Kazakhstan is a goal we must achieve.
We need early and widespread implementation of international technical standards.
This is my main instruction to the Government. This is its direct duty and responsibility to society.
The second challenge is to achieve qualitatively new successes in the regional economy and ensure full participation in the global economy.
We can turn Kazakhstan into a "regional locomotive" of economic development - which it already is in many ways - and make it a successful "player" in the global economy.
We need to have a minimum and maximum programme to search for and develop real Kazakhstani "niches" in the system of the world economy, to participate in major advanced projects with foreign partners, as well as to provide comprehensive and responsible support to the participants of our economy, including through the provision of quality infrastructure services.
The focus should be on the markets of Russia, China, Central Asia, the Caspian and Black Sea regions.
Economic integration within the CIS, EurAsEC, SCO remains the main benchmark for trade.
We propose to go out to create a Eurasian Economic Union of states, to make it beneficial for all our other neighbours to join.
Now, more than ever, the issue of consolidating the efforts of private business and the state to create and conquer new "niches" in world markets with our goods, services and, hopefully, advanced ideas is more relevant than ever.
We need to clearly define the role and place of state holdings in the formation of a competitive economy.
I have said many times that the world market is all taken up, we are not very welcome there. What goods should we export? That is the question. Today we are trading well in oil, gas, mineral resources, and we are exporting wheat. This is good.
But when we talk about industrialisation, it means producing new, different goods that are not dependent on raw materials.
I place the responsibility for solving this task on the Government with the direct participation of the state holdings themselves.
The third objective is to improve the efficiency of the extractive sector.
We intend to continue to pursue a responsible and mutually beneficial energy policy.
Further development of the hydrocarbon sector, attraction of foreign and local investors should be directly linked to diversification of the economy and through this prism the most important tasks of creating new promising industries should be addressed.
We must insist that our foreign partners working on the development of Kazakhstan's richest subsoil turn to the country's needs in a real and serious way and take a decisive part, of course on a market basis, in the diversification of our economy and the social development of Kazakhstan.
I instruct the Government to work with all companies accordingly.
Companies that meet us in this matter will enjoy our support. First of all, we proceed from the national priorities of Kazakhstan.
At the same time, we ensure stability, predictability and long-term interests of our neighbours and international partners to whom Kazakhstan supplies energy resources.
The time has come to develop a holistic strategy to further strengthen Kazakhstan's position in the regional and then global energy space.
The main issue for the development of our energy and petrochemical industries is to increase the profitability of these sectors by increasing the added value of energy products.
The management of priority sectors - petrochemicals, gas resources, export energy corridors - should be particularly effective.
And these are the requirements for all market participants, but, first of all, for the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources and the state holding Samruk.
The fourth task is to ensure the development of the non-resource sector of production and diversification of the economy.
The Government should have its own general strategy for implementing "breakthrough" investment projects in priority non-resource sectors of the economy.
The time has come to assess the efficiency of the implementation of the Industrial and Innovative Development Strategy, taking into account the new economic conditions and priorities.
It is also necessary to formulate requirements and recommendations for the formation of industrial diversification plans. It is time to move from pilot financing of individual projects to large-scale financing of diversification.
This is the responsibility of the Government, Akims, state holdings with the active participation of small and medium-sized businesses.
It is time for us to ask the Government and Akims about the impact of the work we have been doing for the third year to diversify the economy. The state allocates funds for this, we are told about 204 facilities that are in operation today. We need to understand what has been done over these years.
The fifth challenge is to develop modern infrastructure in line with our new role in the regional and global economy.
We need to have a clear vision of the prospects for strategic infrastructure development and significantly improve the quality of management in this area, taking into account, first and foremost, the competitiveness of our domestic companies - consumers of infrastructure services, as well as the interests of our international economic integration.
We need to identify regional centres of economic growth and competitiveness, subordinating their development to the interests of the country's economy as a whole.
Our growing economy requires fundamentally new approaches to the development and management of electricity resources and the creation of the foundations for nuclear power in Kazakhstan.
This is the responsibility of regional akims, ministries of industry and trade, transport and communications, education and science, health, energy and mineral resources, as well as state holdings.
This is the most important task, because the development of the economy depends on the volume of energy supply. And we need to tackle it seriously.
The sixth task is modern education and professional retraining, formation of the foundations of the "smart economy", use of new technologies, ideas and approaches, development of the innovation economy.
The main criterion for the success of the educational reform is to reach a level where any citizen of our country, having received appropriate education and qualifications, can become a sought-after specialist in any country of the world.
We must achieve world-class quality education services across the country.
We need to create an effective system of accreditation and certification of educational institutions at the level of international standards.
Prioritising the development of exact and engineering sciences in higher education is a prerequisite for the new stage of development.
We will pursue a unified state strategy aimed at introducing high technologies and supporting innovation.
Almost all successful modern states, actively integrated into the system of world economic relations, have staked on the "smart economy". And for its creation, it is necessary, first of all, to develop their own human capital.
And this is already the responsibility of all participants in our common Kazakhstani project, but, first of all, of the Ministry of Education and Science and the Ministry of Industry and Trade.
The seventh task is targeted social support and development of the social sphere on market principles.
We will continue our policy of targeted support for those who really need protection, but we will decide on market principles.
We need to help those who are really in need. We should help those who have many children, low-income families, and the disabled. And social support for the rest of the citizens is to create jobs. I would like to remind you that the number of poor people in Kazakhstan has fallen fourfold in four years: from 45 per cent to 12 per cent.
The acquisition of affordable housing and the development of the property market are very important issues. Over 11 million square metres of housing have been commissioned over the two years of the state programme for the development of housing construction. In 2007, 7 million square metres will be commissioned. As you remember, we wanted to commission 12 million square metres in three years, but in fact we will commission 18 million. Already 100 thousand families have received flats, 60 thousand families will receive flats this year , and thus more than half a million Kazakhstani people will become newly settled. The programme is ahead of schedule by 30 per cent. Tell me, when has it ever been like this in Kazakhstan?
Now from what I said at the Security Council. We made this programme and determined who gets mortgage housing. These are young families, teachers, doctors, and then civil servants. And what happens? Even communal housing, which is allocated to disabled war and labour invalids who do not have a penny, even their housing is given to officials who have 3-4 flats! This is a good reason for the Otan party to take all this under control. I instructed, if you remember at the Security Council, to publish all of them by name. Not a single newspaper publishes this information. Why do you think that is? Because our officials are preventing it. Quiet sabotage and resistance to what the President said. How can we tolerate such local officials and those who run these regions?
Targeted support will also be provided on the principles of:
improving the quality of medical services and developing a high-tech healthcare system;
improving the funded pension system and creating jobs.
This is the responsibility of the state, and, above all, of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection and the Ministry of Health.
In addition, I instruct the Government, together with the Astana Akimat, to work out the issue and start accelerated construction of housing in the capital of our country for public sector workers through the system of housing construction savings.
This is necessary to provide qualified personnel for the powerful medical and educational clusters that we are creating here. We must concentrate the best medicine, equipment and doctors in the capital. We will build a new world-class university, where we must attract the best domestic and foreign teachers. Intellectuals, technical and engineering staff should be formed in the capital.
The eighth task is to modernise the political system in accordance with the logic of the new stage of our development.
In 2007, we are embarking on further systemic democratic reforms.
The State Commission for the elaboration and concretisation of the programme of democratic reforms, having summarised the recommendations of political parties, public associations, experts and the opinions of the country's citizens, has prepared specific proposals for further political transformations in the state.
Importantly, these suggestions are not a copying of other people's experiences or abstract theories.
They take into account the needs of our society and Kazakhstan's realities. We are forming our own model of political reforms, our own "Kazakhstani way" of political transit.
And here it should be remembered that the Standing Meeting and then the National Commission, including deputies and political parties, worked on these issues. They travelled to all regions of the country, met with the public, social movements, collected a lot of materials. And the State Commission has summarised all this over the last year. I think we have done a good job. Now we know what our people want.
The peculiarities and characteristic features of our path are the preservation of the presidential form of government, phased reforms, balanced decision-making, nationwide dialogue and consolidation of the main political forces.
To ensure that the proposals are legally formalised, a team of lawyers has already started work and is preparing proposals for both amendments to the country's Constitution and individual laws.
In general, democratic reforms in the coming period will follow the following directions.
Firstly, it is an expansion of the powers of Parliament.
The powers of the Parliament will be strengthened in the formation of the Constitutional Council, the Central Election Commission, the Accounts Committee and, in general, in the issues of approval and control over the implementation of the budget. This will be entirely the prerogative of the Parliament.
The role of Parliament in the formation of the Government will be strengthened.
Secondly, measures will be taken to enhance the role of political parties.
It is proposed to expand the powers of party factions and to finance political parties that will be elected to Parliament from the republican budget. We are considering the issue of expanding the party list in the elections to the Majilis.
Thirdly, one of the most important areas of reform will be the improvement of the judicial and legal system. Starting this year, we are introducing jury trials. A fundamental decision has been taken to transfer the authorisation of arrest to the court. We will gradually move to a modern and open type of judicial procedure.
Fourthly, the development of local representative bodies. We will strengthen maslikhats and give them additional powers. We will strengthen the audit commissions of maslikhats.
In time, district maslikhats may become the basis for the formation of local self-government.
The Accounts Committee needs to consider extending its influence to local, regional budgets so that we have a uniform approach.
The main goal of political transformation for us is to move towards such a modern democratic form of government, which will be able to provide the most effective system of governing society and the state, while maintaining political stability in the country and ensuring all constitutional rights and freedoms of our citizens.
You and I have been struggling for a long time over the law on local self-governance. The simplest and most understandable way: Maslikhats are the bodies of local self-government. With their consent the akim is appointed, they consider the budget. We will strengthen the maslikhats by this. The draft law will have to be updated and adopted.
Strong state power and democracy are not antipodes. Democracy develops only where the rule of law is strictly observed.
And no one questions that Kazakhstan should remain a republic with a presidential form of government.
I call on Parliament, the Government and all civil society institutions to create an effective political system as the main goal of change.
The ninth task is to accelerate administrative reform in line with international practice.
We are building a qualitatively new model of public administration based on the principles of corporate governance, efficiency, transparency and accountability to society.
Our goal is to modernise the Government, create a highly professional public service and an efficient management structure.
The issue of administrative reform is a very complex issue. We need to organise its discussion in the Committees of the Parliament and hold special hearings. It will affect many people.
To improve corporate governance, we created Samruk and gave all our real economy to it. It is necessary for them to increase the volume of capitalisation of national companies, to buy shares of the world's leading companies, to bring advanced technologies here. We collected all the money in Kazyna to also improve corporate governance, to be transparent, open, to work to build modern export-oriented enterprises in Kazakhstan.
This means that these holdings become a partner of the Government. The Government does not interfere in their production activities, but creates conditions for them to work efficiently.
The main task of the Government is to work systematically together with the Parliament to improve the country's legislation, to manage the budget, its spending, the introduction of new technologies, public order, health care, education, the country's security, foreign and domestic trade.
Similarly, you should understand the content of social-entrepreneurial corporations. SPCs will buy out unprofitable enterprises, attract inward investment and develop communications, roads, heat and water supply between the regions.
Akims have to deal with the same things as the Government, only on the ground - health care, education, public order, propaganda of the state policy, local budget, its expenditures.
Here's the short gist of what we have to come to. It will lead to a huge reduction in staff, at the expense of which the salaries of the remaining civil servants will increase. And we will then achieve that compact and professional Government that we have been talking about.
They should be subject to the requirements of the main consumers of public services - directly all citizens and businesses.
I place the responsibility for this task on the Government as a whole.
The tenth task is to promote the achievements and opportunities of the new Kazakhstan in the Central Asian region and in the world community.
Today, we are co-operating with other countries on a wide range of topical issues.
These include ensuring energy security, addressing vital socio-economic issues, fighting terrorism, and combating epidemics and environmental disasters.
We will continue to strengthen our role and authority as a responsible member of regional co-operation and the international community.
This is the responsibility of all political, economic and social leaders, but especially our foreign policy department.
In order to represent the new Kazakhstan in the new world in 10 years, we must respond to the challenges of the new time in a timely and adequate manner.
Therefore, I instruct the Government to consistently address all the above tasks that develop the main provisions of the Strategy-2030 at the New Stage.
To fulfil them, I have identified 30 most important directions of our domestic and foreign policy - this is the strategy of the new stage of Kazakhstan's development.
It is outlined in the second part of my Message today, which will be distributed to those present here and published in print.
Success will be ensured by modern organisation of work and clear coordination between the branches of government, the business community, academic and applied science, non-governmental organisations, the media, and, of course, the support of our fellow citizens.

10 years ago, in 1997, the first Address to the people of Kazakhstan presented a vision of the future of our society and the mission of our state - the Country Development Strategy until 2030. I. STATE POLICY AIMED AT THE SUCCESSFUL INTEGRATION OF KAZAKHSTAN INTO THE WORLD ECONOMY THROUGH THE IDENTIFICATION AND UTILISATION OF EXISTING COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES, AS WELL AS THE FORMATION OF NEW COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES
The first direction - Development and implementation of a holistic strategy aimed at ensuring sustainable competitiveness of the economy.
The global system of the world economy is a well-built and fine-tuned mechanism that works according to its own rules. We need to work according to these rules. We are not expected on the world markets, but we need to become in demand and gain a foothold on them. For this purpose it is necessary:
Firstly, to conduct a systematic analysis, monitoring and assessment of the main sectors of Kazakhstan's economy entering foreign markets in terms of the level of their export profitability and the factors determining it. These are, first of all, high productivity, low overhead costs, availability of resources and materials unavailable to other countries, highly skilled labour force, exclusive technologies, etc. So far such work has not been done in full.
Secondly, to conduct a comparative analysis of competitive industries and sectors of other countries, as well as transnational corporations that participate in the same international markets; to assess the factors that cause Kazakhstan's exporters and sectors to lag behind or, on the contrary, give them comparative advantages.
Third, assess the pros and cons of specific export industries and identify areas where the existing advantages should be maintained and where the existing problems should be eliminated.
At the same time, we must assess the effectiveness of actions already taken to develop promising industries, including those for the domestic market, and consider opportunities to develop their export potential.
Fourth, based on such a systemic analysis, we should develop breakthrough macro projects that can change the structure of industry, with significant added value, multiplier effect, export and resource-saving potential.
Fifth, it is important to organise targeted systematic support for the entry of Kazakhstani business into foreign markets.
I instruct the Government to develop and implement a holistic Strategy for achieving a qualitatively new level of competitiveness and export opportunities for the economy.
On this basis, an appropriate Programme of Action, a system of evaluation of intermediate results and its implementation as a whole should be prepared. It should contain recommendations for large, medium and small businesses, information on necessary legislative changes and real measures of state assistance to specific sectors, prepared jointly with the National Union of Entrepreneurs "Atameken". Based on these results, we will be able to develop modern approaches to prospective restructuring of our economy.
The National Council on Competitiveness and Exports, which I instruct the Government to create, should become a coordinating and working body.
The second direction - Search, conquest and creation of Kazakhstan's "niches" in the system of the world economy
Firstly, we need to expand the areas where we can already capitalise on our achievements and successes. The focus should be on the markets of Russia, China, Central Asia, the Caspian and Black Sea regions.
Secondly, it is necessary to accelerate the search for new, as well as to consider, at first glance, not particularly attractive or non-traditional export "niches". Our external partners can also be involved in this work on mutually beneficial terms.
Thirdly, the development of new industries in Kazakhstan, including high-tech industries that can achieve international competitiveness, will help develop new export niches.
For example, last year, you know, in Northern Kazakhstan we opened a unique bioethanol production facility, which has no analogues in our CIS neighbours.
Construction of the first integrated petrochemical complex in the Atyrau region will begin this year, which will enable the further development of world-class petrochemical production facilities. And the Atyrau Refinery can already produce petrol and diesel fuel meeting European standards.
Fourth, we should analyse the possibilities of creating and developing new industrial production facilities in border areas where our neighbouring states have already established commercial, industrial, financial and service structures. Such breakthrough projects can be linked, for example, to the growth of the economies of China and South-East Asia. On the border with China, it would be advisable to create enterprises that could process Kazakhstani raw materials and supply Chinese duty-free zones with these products, as well as with energy, fuel, etc. We could also develop enterprises there. In the future, we could also develop there the sphere of providing various services - transportation, distribution of goods, logistics, using the capabilities of the International Centre for Cross-Border Cooperation "Khorgos" and creating a trade and economic zone "Khorgos-Eastern Gate".
The government and, first and foremost, the Ministry of Industry and Trade, as well as state-owned holdings, are obliged to develop and launch a programme for the expansion and development of export "niches" with Kazakhstani goods and services, with responsible recommendations for participants in our economy.
Third direction - Participation in large and "breakthrough" projects
Our economic achievements have defined Kazakhstan's leadership in the Central Asian economy.
Now we have the strength to turn Kazakhstan into a "regional locomotive" of economic development and make it a successful "player" in the world economy.
Firstly. The government should create a system for informing our companies about promising regional projects and assisting them to participate in such projects and obtain state contracts on a competitive basis. These can be high-tech production, infrastructure and other projects.
Secondly, we need to stimulate co-operation between our large corporations and transnational companies in order to develop specific "breakthrough" projects.
Third, Kazakhstan will develop the integration of regional financial markets around the financial centre in Almaty, create commodity markets in the region based on modern technologies of international trade, for example, a grain exchange.
I instruct the Government, all relevant bodies and institutions, including state holdings, to create favourable conditions for the transformation of Kazakhstan into a regional "centre for the provision of goods and services", but most importantly, to take concrete measures to ensure the participation of Kazakhstani companies in major regional economic projects.
Fourth direction - Focusing the activities of state holdings and organising their work in accordance with international standards
We must not allow our state holdings to turn into unmanageable multi-profile conglomerates, which, in most cases, are not competitive on the international market. We must also avoid the danger of their transformation into banal financial "troughs" with a certain system of privileges. Attention should also be paid to the fact that state holdings should not replace the activities of their member national companies and organisations, but, on the contrary, consolidate these economic activities at a new level, overcome the duplication of functions, unproductive internal competition and their closed nature, increase their efficiency and transparency.
First of all, state holdings should take their leading place in ensuring competitiveness and implementation of the national strategy aimed at successful integration of Kazakhstan into the world economy.
Firstly, I instruct state holdings and relevant government agencies to critically analyse the existing analytical, marketing and technological developments and determine the next steps, specifying the final results and the timeframe for their achievement. The formation of "niches" for our exporters and full-fledged international integration requires timely clear tasks and a plan for the implementation of specific "breakthrough" projects.
Secondly, state holdings should actively work with international companies to create joint projects and facilitate their entry into Kazakhstan. Joint work in non-resource sectors is especially important for us.
Thirdly, state holdings should play their role in the diversification of the economy, involve in this process, stimulate and support Kazakhstan's small and medium-sized businesses.
Fourth, in order to solve these problems, it is necessary to develop a plan for restructuring state holdings as a single organism, as well as to create correspondingly focused, fully functioning, efficient, flexible and transparent internal structures. In this regard, it is advisable to conduct a functional analysis, efficiency analysis and profiling of the structures that make up each state holding, and then determine which assets remain under the management of each state holding and how they will be developed, and which ones should be transferred to the competitive environment.
"Samruk."
Firstly, Samruk's main objective is to manage public sector enterprises in the economy to ensure that they increase in value.
Secondly, I instruct the management of Samruk to work out a unified strategy for its development, defining the activities of its state-owned companies, at an accelerated pace.
Thirdly, Samruk should use its capabilities and resources to fulfil those tasks and projects that will give competitive advantages to all domestic consumers of infrastructure services and relevant sectors of the economy in foreign markets. In other words, enterprises and the population, in the end, should receive, of course, higher quality and, if possible, inexpensive energy, railway, telecommunication and household services.
Fourth, Samruk should develop a clear scheme for attracting funds from accumulative pension funds, development institutions and private investors, both Kazakhstani and foreign, to secure its strategy.
"Kazyna".
"Kazyna should formulate and implement a common strategy for the activities of all institutions and organisations within its structure. The goal for all should be the same - to provide assistance and incentives to increase the competitiveness and export opportunities of small, medium and large businesses in Kazakhstan, to ensure international "breakthroughs" and favourable conditions for the formation of export "niches" and infrastructure development.

Firstly, the Kazyna Fund should provide modern services to develop competitiveness and support exports of the most promising entrepreneurs and industries - from financing applied research to promoting Kazakhstani goods in foreign and domestic markets. The Fund should become an operator of the state on the issues of service support for exports.
Secondly, Kazyna should identify how it can incentivise the introduction of new technologies and the development of applied science to enhance the competitiveness and export capabilities of priority sectors of the economy and the companies concerned.
Thirdly, it would be advisable for the Kazyna Fund to assist our advanced enterprises, and mainly non-mining industries, to improve their trading conditions abroad and increase their export access, including through structured financing, export credits, export insurance and so on.
Fourthly, it is necessary to comprehensively understand the process of venture financing of new industries on a competitive basis, which would win their niche in the international market and firmly maintain their positions there. Today, Kazyna should have a wide range of tools to create new competitive industries and sectors of Kazakhstan's economy.
Fifth, one of the important activities of the Fund should be to attract relevant international companies to joint ventures with export potential.
Sixth, the Fund should actively attract domestic and foreign business to the special economic and industrial zones and technoparks created exclusively for export purposes.
Seventh, it is necessary to establish a Fund of Funds this year, including with foreign financial institutions.
"KazAgro
Similar approaches should also form the basis for the work of the KazAgro National Holding Company.
Firstly, the main task of KazAgro is to systematically address the issues of increasing the level of agricultural productivity, preventing land degradation, strengthening the efficiency of water and other natural resources use in the country due to the use of, among other things, outdated agro-technologies, slow development of agrarian science, as well as the fragmentation of small peasant farms.
Secondly, KazAgro, within the framework of the set tasks, should conduct a qualitative analysis of all sectors of our agriculture, identify niches that need to be developed in the first place. For example, there is a new market of agricultural products that is actively developing in the world - these are environmentally friendly products, new productions, etc.
Thirdly, KazAgro needs to develop and implement systems for financing existing and new agricultural producers with export potential in the near future. Such financing should be targeted and provide for the replacement of outdated agro-technologies and the creation of a high-tech agro-industry. It may be necessary to involve second-tier banks as operators in this process.
One of the main tasks of all state holdings, their member national companies and other organisations remains the streamlining of their activities through the introduction of international practices of corporate governance, accountability and transparency.
They should become a model of corporate behaviour for all businesses in Kazakhstan.
Firstly, the work of state holdings should be built in accordance with the Corporate Governance Code.
Secondly, it is necessary to increase the level of transparency in the activities of state holdings. The society should have information about the strategies of these companies, their ownership structure, results of financial and economic activities, etc.
Thirdly, the economic activities of state holdings, personnel recruitment, etc. should be based on transparent competitive procedures.
Fourth, effective Boards of Directors should be in place to drive strategy and effectively oversee management, finance and performance.
Fifth, we expect that an annual audit of the performance of state holdings, which will be conducted with the involvement of an independent auditor with an impeccable reputation, will help to ensure a clear system of transparency and public evaluation of the activities of these holdings.
Such principles should govern the work of all state holdings.
I instruct the management of state holdings to submit their development concepts and new structure to the President for approval no later than August 2007. After approval of the strategy and structure, Samruk, Kazyna and KazAgro should start implementing the set tasks, and their managers will be personally responsible for the results.
Track Five - Significantly improve the efficiency and macroeconomic returns of the extractive sector
We intend to continue to pursue a responsible and mutually beneficial energy policy.
Further development of the hydrocarbon sector, attraction of foreign and local investors should be directly linked to diversification of the economy and through this prism the most important tasks of creating new promising industries should be addressed.
The government should raise the issue with major investors working with our natural resources about their greater and more concrete contribution to the industrialisation of Kazakhstan, initiating, if necessary, an appropriate draft Law.
First and foremost, we proceed from Kazakhstan's national priorities. At the same time, we ensure the stability, predictability and long-term interests of our neighbours and international partners.
The time has come to develop a holistic strategy to further strengthen Kazakhstan's position in the regional energy space.
Firstly, the Government, together with state holdings, should take concrete measures to stimulate and ensure access of Kazakhstan's energy exporters to international markets.
Secondly, the Government should formulate a new strategy for the gas industry and create a legislative framework for its implementation.
Third, in order to ensure uninterrupted energy supplies, enter into intensive negotiations with our neighbours and convince them that it is advisable to establish an integrated system of energy networks of the states of the region in Central Asia, as well as an Energy Security Council that would facilitate the creation of a market system that would ensure regional and international energy security. This is in the interests of all countries in the region.
Fourthly, an effective legislative framework must be put in place to make wise use of our natural resources and address the problems of environmental pollution, uncontrolled importation of outdated and "dirty" technologies, inefficient use of renewable resources, etc.
It is necessary to tighten control over compliance with environmental legislation when developing oil fields on the Caspian shelf. The government should work on the introduction of international certificates based on the "Green Oil" principle, which requires compliance with strict environmental standards in hydrocarbon production.
The main issue of our energy and petrochemicals development is to increase the profitability of these sectors by increasing the added value of energy products.The management of priority sectors - petrochemicals, gas resources, export energy routes - should be particularly effective.
First, the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources should create and implement programmes to modernise and re-equip oil and gas refineries and create new petrochemical production facilities. We must develop high value-added, associated and related industries in the oil and gas sector.
The Government needs to staff this Ministry with modern-type personnel capable of professionally solving the most serious issues of the energy sector - the main branch of the country's economy at this stage.
Secondly, the Ministry of Energy, together with other state bodies, should prepare a programme of practical measures for transition to energy-saving technologies. The introduction of such technologies and programmes for saving and rational use of natural resources should be implemented in compliance with the principles of optimal combination of economic, social and environmental factors. Such a programme could include, for example, introduction of strict state control over disposal and recycling of energy production and consumption waste, fulfilment of contractual obligations by entrepreneurs to comply with environmental standards, introduction of low-waste technologies, etc.
Third, by the end of the year, the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources should prepare a new development strategy aimed at balancing production and exports in the oil and gas industry and, at the same time, at exploring and finding new hydrocarbon deposits and new methods of utilising oil and gas resources.
Fourthly, it is necessary to improve the legislative framework and to carry out comprehensive monitoring of subsoil use and fulfilment of subsoil users' obligations. The government should eliminate bureaucratic delays, reduce the list of permits and simplify the procedure for granting rights to subsoil users.
Fifth, the Government should improve the systems of control over the contractual obligations of large enterprises to meet social obligations and to replace skilled foreign labour with Kazakhstani specialists.
Track Six - A New Level of Financial System Resilience and Competitiveness in a Liberalised Environment
Firstly, our banks must be prepared to compete in the local market, regional and international projects. We have eliminated a number of restrictions on non-residents' access to our financial system as part of the negotiation process for Kazakhstan's accession to the WTO.
Second, conditions should be created for the provision of market-oriented support to promising sectors of the economy by the banking system of Kazakhstan and strengthen the banking presence in regional economic projects, including within the framework of public-private partnerships.
Thirdly, to address the important issue of attracting capital from strong second-tier banks to implement national-scale projects, especially energy, infrastructure and breakthrough projects.
Fourthly, it is also necessary to return once again to the issue of removing unjustified restrictions in the sphere of capital movement. This issue should be considered with taking into account the need to maintain an optimal aggregate external debt of Kazakhstan. Our banks rely too much on external financing, which may lead to uncontrolled growth of the country's total external debt.
Fifthly, we need to create an efficient stock market. Its development is impossible without attracting the population to actively invest their savings in securities. It is necessary to carry out large-scale work on the appropriate training of the population in the basics of investment literacy.
Sixth, a factor in the development of the e-commerce system will be the further improvement of the legislative framework for expanding the infrastructure of electronic banking services.
The Government, together with the Financial Supervisory Agency, should prepare a strategy and the necessary legislative support for the above work.
Seventh direction - Accession to the WTO on terms favourable to Kazakhstan
Strengthening Kazakhstan's competitive position in the global economy will largely be determined by its accession to the World Trade Organisation.We have been consistently addressing this task for several years and are close to completion.
Firstly, in order to take into account Kazakhstan's national interests, it is necessary to bring Kazakhstan's legislation into compliance with the norms of binding WTO agreements by the end of the year.
Secondly, in the process of Kazakhstan's accession to the WTO, the Government should maintain an acceptable level of domestic state support for the agricultural sector and implement appropriate adaptation measures to prepare industrial enterprises for effective functioning under WTO conditions.
Thirdly, we need to develop real, effective and systematic measures to improve customs administration and ensure that customs professionals meet modern requirements. We must pursue a policy of opening up the economy, reducing customs barriers between the countries of the region and establishing a uniform level of external tariffs in the region. In recent years, the government has allocated considerable sums to our customs system for these and other purposes.
Fourthly, it is necessary to accelerate the process of transition of all legal entities to the International Financial Reporting Standards.
Fifthly, the Government together with the Atameken Union should soon prepare appropriate recommendations for our industrialists and entrepreneurs from all sectors of the economy.

II. STATE POLICY AIMED AT MANAGING THE GROWTH AND SUSTAINABILITY OF KAZAKHSTAN'S ECONOMY THROUGH DIVERSIFICATION, INFRASTRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT AND CREATION OF FOUNDATIONS FOR HIGH-TECH FURTHER INDUSTRIALISATION
The eighth direction - Diversification of the economy and development of the non-resource sector
The government should pay special attention to the implementation of "breakthrough" investment projects in priority non-resource sectors of the economy.
We must move from "growth of savings" to "growth management", which means, first of all, pursuing an investment policy aimed at developing infrastructure and further industrialisation of Kazakhstan's economy.
Firstly, the Government should create conditions for the development of new technological and backbone industries with a real multiplier effect. Such industries may include, for example, oil and gas machine building; production of special alloys; production of biochemical and petrochemical products; processing industries of food, textile, agricultural products, production of construction materials and others.
Secondly, in the field of agricultural policy, the Government should implement programmes for the sustainable development of the agro-industrial complex by increasing the productivity and profitability of its sectors and developing the national competitive advantages of domestic products.
Thirdly, to improve the legislative framework and to carry out comprehensive monitoring of subsoil use and fulfilment of subsoil users' obligations.
Fourthly, the Government should prepare effective measures to develop Kazakhstan's service market in subsoil use, machine building and heavy industry.
I instruct the Government and state holdings in dialogue with the Union of Entrepreneurs "Atameken" to formulate requirements and recommendations for the largest companies to formulate their industrial diversification strategies.
Ninth direction - Implementation of a unified state strategy aimed at introducing high technologies and supporting innovations
Firstly, we need to actively and thoughtfully implement technology transfer based on our competitive advantages. It is necessary to promote the creation of a network of design bureaus and design organisations that will both import ready-made technologies and refine them, and introduce domestic scientific developments into production.
Secondly, it is necessary to create structures to support the financing of projects in the sphere of high technologies, including on the basis of venture financing. The best developments of Kazakhstani scientists should not be allowed to go abroad.
Thirdly, it is necessary to stimulate the innovation activity of Kazakhstani business. The greatest efforts in research and development activities should come from the private sector.
Fourthly, it is necessary to systematise the state order for research works so that the results of these works are in demand by the real sector of the economy.
Fifth, it is necessary to promote the development of the technology sector by strengthening the protection of intellectual property and trade marks. It is necessary to create a bank of innovations and patents, available for review and financing. This is Kazyna's task.
Track 10 - Formation and launch of regional centres for economic growth and competitiveness
Coordinated formation of regional centres and "points" of economic growth and competitiveness through priority development of leading cities with significant economic potential plays an important role in ensuring regional development. The government needs to identify such centres by studying their potential for development as growth centres for the country's economy as a whole.
The most important centre of economic growth has, of course, become our capital Astana, having transformed in just a decade from a provincial city into a modern metropolis with huge opportunities, and not only for Kazakhstanis.
We need to further develop these capabilities if we are to really compete with the recognised capitals of the world.
First, we need to start building at least two new centres for Astana - on the right bank and on the left bank in the south-eastern direction.
Secondly, it is important to accelerate the pace of construction of the new scientific complex of the National Biotechnology Centre in Astana.
Third, the Government should continue to implement the programme to create a medical cluster in Astana on the basis of newly introduced world-class republican scientific innovative medical centres.
Fourth, a Eurasian Water Centre should be established in Astana to address the issues of water resources research and protection on the continent.
I instruct the Akim of Astana and the Government to identify specific indicators of socio-economic development that can be achieved in the medium and long term.
The issue of socio-entrepreneurial corporations is relevant.
We have set a goal to achieve spatial integration of Kazakhstan, ensuring infrastructure development, labour mobility and growth of competitiveness of regions, and on their basis to form "points of growth".
First, this task should be implemented taking into account the transformation of Kazakhstan into a regional "economic locomotive" and a centre of modern services and high-tech industry. Using the process of consolidation of the public and private sectors, it is necessary to create specific "growth centres" on the basis of targeted regional development plans - for example, Astana, Akmola and Karaganda regions, taking into account the already established Saryarka SPK.
Secondly, such "centres of economic growth" should be provided with all the necessary social infrastructure with a focus on education - preschool, secondary and vocational education.
Thirdly, "growth poles" should also be created on the basis of the development of a network of social and entrepreneurial corporations (SBC). Their activity implies the implementation of investment and innovation projects in the agricultural, transport and logistics and other sectors. The government should transfer the necessary state property and assets to SBCs and solve the issues of development of corporations with the participation of entrepreneurs.
The government and akims should jointly prepare specific proposals for the location of industrial enterprises and industrial zones in these centres, taking into account our plans for the development of industry, trade and high technology.
Eleventh direction - Development of strategic infrastructure on the basis of public-private partnership, as well as improving the quality of management in this area
I instruct the Government together with akims to prepare a plan for the development of modern infrastructure, subordinate to the tasks:
- our integration into the international infrastructure market;
- development of centres of regional economic activity;
- technological interaction between different modes of transport;
- reducing costs for businesses and citizens.
For its implementation, we should actively use the capabilities of state holdings and form an infrastructure development mechanism based on public-private partnership.
Firstly, we need to purposefully maintain, upgrade and expand our transport infrastructure. We need to maximise the country's transit potential, and for this we need to integrate our transport system into the global one.
Secondly, we need to actively develop the air transport sector. We need to bring the infrastructure of our airports and the aviation industry in line with the requirements of the national economy and the international level. It is necessary to create all conditions for the development of competition in the local aviation market in order to improve the quality and safety of air services and reduce their cost. Air transport should become more accessible to citizens.
A corresponding programme for the development of this infrastructure should be developed by the end of 2007.
Thirdly, we are talking about the need to modernise the country's railway network through the gradual transfer of railway transportation and management to a market-based system.
The establishment and expansion of a network of railway transport and logistics centres should also be initiated to match the current and future level of demand for such transport services. The railway industry should meet global standards for safety, speed of delivery and service, and tariffs should be in line with reasonable industry requirements.
The Ministry of Transport and Communications together with the state holding Samruk should revise the current Rules of Railway Transport and develop new ones corresponding to a higher level of economic development.
Fourthly, systematic work on demonopolisation and development of free competition in the telecommunications industry is to be carried out. It is necessary to finally complete the work on tariff re-balancing so that other investors will come into this sphere. It is necessary to create conditions for reducing the cost of Internet services, thereby increasing the penetration of the global network into our schools, businesses and homes.
Fifth, we need to take an equally responsible approach to the development of water transport infrastructure. Intensive development of the Caspian shelf requires new ports and sea transport vessels. It is expedient to implement programmes to create new shipyard capacities and modernise existing sea and river ports.
Sixth, development of road transport infrastructure. Last year, the implementation of the Road Sector Development Programme until 2012 was launched. For the first time, the government is allocating almost USD 10 billion to finance the road sector. The development of this infrastructure will also improve traffic safety and reduce road injuries.
The government should prepare a strategy within six months to bring the main motorways of international importance in line with international standards. In addition, as part of the development of the transport and logistics cluster, a motorway through Kazakhstan should be built to connect Western Europe with Western China.
We also need to accelerate the expansion of local road networks, improving access to Kazakhstan's most remote communities.
Twelfth track - Developing electricity resources and laying the foundations for nuclear energy
Today the most urgent issue is to provide electricity to South Kazakhstan, Karaganda, Aktobe, Kostanay regions and the city of Almaty.
First, it is necessary to solve the problem of electricity distribution between energy-surplus and energy-deficient regions in a balanced way, using the capacities of neighbouring countries and switching to energy-saving technologies.
Secondly, it is necessary to consistently modernise the power industry, address the problems of wear and tear and capacity shortages, and create conditions for the development of new industries, expansion and reconstruction of existing equipment and power transmission networks.
Thirdly, diversification of energy sources requires the development of nuclear power to provide resources for sustainable development of the entire country. It is necessary to develop a feasibility study for the construction of a nuclear power plant in Kazakhstan.
Fourth, consideration should be given to establishing an energy exchange, following the example of Norway and Sweden, with neighbouring states in an energy union.
I instruct the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources to develop by the end of 2007 a set of measures to increase the capacity of existing power plants, build new generating capacities and optimise the electricity network in order to meet the energy needs of the regions. Finally, we need concrete steps and a systematic approach to solving the problem of energy supply in the south of the country.
Important areas of work should also include economic and administrative measures aimed at stimulating the efficient use of electricity, as well as the development of mechanisms for introducing energy-saving technologies, including knowledge-intensive technologies, into the energy sector.
Thirteenth area - Consistent actions to support small and medium-sized businesses
First, the Government should analyse where and why legislative, administrative and bureaucratic obstacles to business initiative appear, reduce them as much as possible, and eliminate unjustified reporting of small and medium-sized business structures to the state. It is also necessary to improve tax legislation so that it fully stimulates the development of entrepreneurship and facilitates the exit of business "from the shadow".
Secondly, we must complete the work to create a fair competitive environment and equal conditions for all economic players. I instruct the Government to conduct a comprehensive revision of the antimonopoly legislation and create clear mechanisms for identifying the facts of restriction of competition and collusion between market participants, preventing "hidden" monopolisation of the basic sectors of our economy, as well as appropriate recommendations on the application of penalties.
Third, we should reduce the spheres of natural monopolies as much as possible, we need to renew the existing and develop new programmes for restructuring and developing competitive relations in the relevant sectors. In order to regulate and control the sectors of the economy with remaining natural monopolies - telecommunications and air navigation, railway transport and ports, electricity, oil and gas pipelines, and housing and utilities - we need to create independent sectoral regulators. These structures, headed by collegial bodies, will combine the functions of tariff and technical regulation.
Fourth, improve the process of creating new enterprises and companies. For example, within the framework of the "one window" system, it is necessary to create such conditions that an entrepreneur can register a company within two or three days.
Fifth, for sustainable and dynamic economic growth, we need to make more active use of the resources of the state and state-owned companies as a catalyst for creating demand for high quality products and services of small and medium-sized businesses in Kazakhstan on a public and competitive basis.
Sixth, it is advisable to develop special programmes for the development of new industries on a transparent and public competitive basis, where the best business ideas will receive financial and technical support for the formation of new businesses, for example, to cover legal and consulting costs. This is a task, I believe, for the Kazyna Fund.
Fourteenth track - Early and widespread implementation of technical standards in line with international requirements
Kazakhstan's full participation in competition in the international economic arena will require the fulfilment of international technical standards.
Technical standardisation should be seen not only as a tool to ensure the quality of products and services, but also as a prerequisite for ensuring the competitiveness of our goods and services in the global economy.
Standardisation of Kazakhstan's economy should be carried out on the basis of the latest achievements of science, technology and practical experience and determine optimal solutions to many general economic, sectoral and internal production tasks.
I charge the Ministry of Industry and Commerce:
Firstly, to analyse the results of already existing developments in the implementation of the law on technical regulation;

Secondly, within six months, to put the work on the implementation of international standardisation procedures and rules into practice.
Fifteenth track - Strengthening private property and contractual arrangements
I would like to once again place special emphasis on the need to continue work on the implementation of a holistic programme to fully strengthen the institution of private property and contractual relations.
Firstly, the development of a legal framework and law enforcement practice in this area is undoubtedly a priority. I am in charge of developing an appropriate package of legislative acts. I believe that the draft laws "On state registration of rights to immovable property and transactions with it" (new version), "On introducing amendments and additions to some legislative acts of the Republic of Kazakhstan on state registration of rights to immovable property and transactions with it" will be adopted soon.
Secondly, it is necessary to foster respect for the institution of private property and contractual relations at all levels, including using all possible levers of the state, educational and judicial systems, etc. I also count on the constructive role of our civil society institutions, since strengthening the institution of private property is at the same time creating the foundations for guaranteeing human rights and freedoms.
Third, the Government should take appropriate measures to improve contractual relations that clearly define the rules of public-private partnership.
The sixteenth direction - Forming the foundations for further industrialisation of Kazakhstan
We must manage economic growth on the basis of a policy of further industrialisation of Kazakhstan that meets the modern requirements of the international market.
First, it is necessary to carry out an analysis, assessing the full scale of the problem of equipping the economy with production capacities and the depreciation of fixed capital in the country, and to prepare a specific programme of action aimed at radical renewal of capital equipment, production infrastructure and technological processes.
Second, to identify the most priority industries and enterprises and the system of priority measures for their industrialisation on a modern basis.
Third, to develop instruments of state stimulation of the private sector, which should play a leading role in the process of further industrialisation.
I instruct the Government to carry out work organically linked to the Strategy of achieving a qualitatively new level of competitiveness and export opportunities of the economy by the end of 2008 in order to develop the industrial-innovation strategy.
III. STATE POLICY AIMED AT ENSURING INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS OF EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL RETRAINING THAT ARE IN LINE WITH THE DYNAMICS AND PROSPECTS OF THE LABOUR MARKET DEVELOPMENT
Seventeenth axis - Bringing primary and secondary education and retraining closer to world standards
We must achieve world-class quality education services across the country.
Firstly, to eliminate 3-shift education. In the next three years, 100 new schools should be built in the regions of Kazakhstan on the basis of public-private partnership.
Secondly, to create a unified system for assessing the effectiveness of training, the level of knowledge and skills of each trainee.
Thirdly, to develop the practice of online learning and to create a national educational television.
Fourthly, introduce additional hours or subjects in science, primarily maths and computer science, into the curriculum, as well as a system of special science classes. The government should develop mechanisms to attract the necessary investments in this direction.
Fifth, attract foreign English teachers to schools, so that any average school can provide children with the opportunity to learn a foreign language at the highest level.
Sixth, consider introducing a system of state competitions to award grants to high-performing schools, which would be provided, for example, in the form of scholarship funding for students from low-income families. This would enable them to further their education in more prestigious and advanced educational institutions.
Improving the system for evaluating and rewarding the work of the best teachers is worth particular scrutiny.
Eighteenth axis - Introduction of certification of educational institutions at the level of international standards, priority development of exact and engineering sciences in the sphere of higher education
Firstly, the Government should introduce a system of attestation of educational institutions at the level of international standards, allowing an objective assessment of the quality of education in each HEI. Consideration should also be given to attracting reputable agencies for international accreditation of higher education organisations.
Secondly, as part of the structural reform of science, it is advisable to merge a number of academic research institutions with advanced universities, which can serve as a basis for the creation of universities combining educational and research work.
Third, the Government should develop an appropriate regulatory legal framework for the development of specialised training programmes and science-applied centres for exact and engineering sciences.
Fourth, the Ministry of Education and Science and other relevant structures of the Government should prepare a programme for the development of scientific and technological training and monitor its implementation on the principles of strengthening inter-sectoral coordination of scientific, design and technological work with the efficient use of financial resources and overcoming the duplication of scientific and applied research.
Fifth, we should more actively engage foreign public development institutions and academic centres, and encourage private sector involvement and investment in mathematics and science education.
Sixth, as part of the strategy to increase the number of qualified teaching staff and engineering and pedagogical personnel, foreign scientists and teachers should be actively recruited to those areas of education that are of most interest to us.
Seventh, specialised areas of study are to be created that focus on information technology and new forms of information dissemination.
Nineteenth track - Forming the foundations of the "smart economy"
Almost all successful modern states, actively integrated into the system of world economic relations, have staked on the "smart economy". And for its creation, it is necessary, first of all, to develop their "human capital".
At the initial stage, we should pay attention to the following:
Firstly, to introduce requirements and form the appropriate infrastructure to regularly update the publicly available knowledge base required for our new economy in line with the level of global technological development as a whole.
Secondly, provide direct support for the creation of innovation-education consortia for the implementation of educational programmes and scientific-applied research.
Thirdly, expand the practice of joint participation of research institutes and universities in tenders for government or private sector orders for R&D, grants, joint scientific publications, etc., as well as the practice of joint participation of research institutes and universities in competitions.
Fourthly, to recommend to the companies-suppliers of new technologies mandatory training of Kazakhstani personnel to work with these technologies.
Fifthly, it is necessary to create appropriate prerequisites for entrepreneurs to be interested in the scientific and technological security and competitiveness of the private sector. The fulfilment of contractual obligations of entrepreneurs to train Kazakhstani specialists should also be strictly monitored.
IV. MODERN SOCIAL POLICY: PEOPLE'S DEMANDS AND NEEDS AND JOB CREATION AT THE CENTRE OF ATTENTION
Two years ago, we set a course for consistent social modernisation. And we have achieved a lot.
The main thing for us is to create all the necessary conditions for the people of Kazakhstan to realise important and understandable life principles:
- providing for the family;
- home ownership;
- children's education;
- health promotion;
- building up savings for retirement.
From our previous experience and from the experience of other countries around the world, we must draw two fundamental conclusions.
First: Social support of the population by the state can be effective only if it is targeted and targeted. The state is obliged and actually takes responsibility for supporting only those members of society who really need this help - and these are, first of all, children, mothers with many children, veterans, and the disabled.
Second: The most effective social policy has been and remains the policy of motivation to productive labour and the creation of new jobs. We need, first of all, to create real incentives for people who, for one reason or another, have lost their jobs to return to work, to give them the opportunity to get a new profession. In addition, we need to resume popularisation and active promotion of working professions among young people, especially in industry.
Twentieth axis - Consistent policy on housing affordability and property market development
